editions.summary: REGIME TRANSITION, one day before CPI. Iran declared all Hormuz transit 'temporarily unavailable' (IRNA, Sunday) and the President reinstated 'THE IRANIAN BLOCKADE' with a 20% cargo levy Monday — two formal closure acts. WTI spiked ~9% to ~$77.8*, THROUGH the $75 supply threshold: the supply dimension re-flags and the composite transitions to Stagflationary Pressure / Supply Easing, ending the 14-session Residual/Normalised run — the first label change since 22 June. SEMANTIC CAVEAT (audit H2, now live in production): 'Supply Easing' is the $75-90 level-band's name, coined during June's DOWNWARD traversal; today's direction is re-escalation upward through the band. The label is mechanical; the direction disagrees with its name; the threshold re-basing protocol escalates to priority. Robustness collapsed to 0.23 LOW on transition (tenure 1; risk at B=0.05 with VIX 17.1; growth at 0.00) — the formula behaving as designed. Weight revision #4: escalation 46->54, the first MAJORITY of the series (base 20, stalemate 18, resolution 8). Both tracks moved together for the first time — realized transmission finally confirmed what forward risk priced. Governance win: the contested Hormuz read RESOLVED — verified count 13 tankers vs 33/day (61% reduction); the '87% disrupted' claim was a garble of '13 tankers,' and Friday's refusal to arm the channel on it is vindicated. The chokepoint arming test is now live on the first post-closure count. editions.summary: THE LABEL'S FIRST FULL WEEK OPENED WITH THE PAPER FRAMEWORK GONE AND THE ACTS UNCHANGED. The June 17 memorandum of understanding — collapsed in practice since the route fights, but the last document either side could point to — technically expired today, and Trump said he is not interested in extending it; fighting flared anew in Lebanon. Oil took the cue: WTI rose 2.6% (84.54 derived), Brent settled just below $91, Treasuries sold off (10Y 4.68), and gold printed 4,472.90 (futures basis, flagged) — while equities merely inched lower near their records, Industrials leading, Meta -3.5% dragging Communication Services. HOLD #8: the expiry is a paper-status change and 'not extending' is a declaration — the acts-only bar does not move on either; the Lebanon flare is logged, not weighted, until the wire supplies a subject and a magnitude. GOVERNANCE: the §5 anchoring check fired on stalemate (ten editions at 14) and halted the append — reviewed both directions (expiry + 3.0 mb/d flow print raise the paper case; ten escalatory-act editions run against it; nothing executed toward either exit) and RECONFIRMED at 14 with operator ratification; the cell moves on an executed reopening step or a strike wave/kinetic closure. Barclays' flow print — Hormuz net exports 3.0 mb/d in the week to August 7, from 4.4 — is the first strait number in weeks, direction WORSE, filed to the count-model. THE CONSUMER MOVED FROM SIGNAL TO THESIS: Hatzius formally called the slowdown (real spending 1-1.5% in H2 as the tax-refund surge fades) — the sell-side ratifying Friday's UMich/retail turn — with Walmart, Home Depot and Target testifying this week. The A-2 view names the venue change: the divergence thesis rests, and the evidence moves from the strait to the household. Weekend container reset absorbed cleanly (engine hash verified, archive restored, r48 unpacked, A-2 skill re-read). editions.summary: THE THREAT INFLATION TURNED ON THE MEDIATOR — AND THE LONG BOND, NOT THE STRAIT, WAS THE SESSION'S PRESSURE. Trump threatened to 'bomb the s*** out of' Oman if it interferes with Hormuz, said he is in no rush and doesn't see the war ending soon, promised more economic pain for Iran; a senior Iranian official told Reuters Tehran may shift to a 'full offensive' posture. Words, all of it, both directions — HOLD #9; fourteen revisions, nine holds, none on rhetoric. THE TAPE MOVED ON TWO OTHER THINGS. The chips broke: the semiconductor gauge -5.5%, the Nasdaq 100 -1.7%, the S&P 7,691.76 (-0.69%) — this year's best corner pummeled a day after memory names surged (Micron back above $1,000 Monday, -4% class Tuesday; Fabrinet -9%). And the long end repriced: the 30Y printed 5.31 Monday — the highest since June 2007 — and held near that 19-year high Tuesday with the 10Y at 4.70, bond anxiety over inflation AND debt pinning yields; the 5.2371 carry had run 7bp low — the expiry priced in duration first. Oil settled ~85 (2-week high), Brent ~91, the SPR at its lowest since 1982. THE STRAIT'S COUNT FINALLY PRINTED, TWICE: MarineTraffic/Kpler crossings fell from 19 to 3 in five days — three vessels Sunday against ~130 pre-war daily, 'essentially stopped' — and with Barclays' 3.0 mb/d the hormuz field moves from a 58-session-stale 61 to 85 on a flow basis (count-basis ~97 logged). Tested first: the classifier is invariant at 61/85/97 — Supply Shock reads oil — a sourcing correction, not a classification event, closing the run's longest EVENT_DRIVEN carry. GOVERNANCE — A NEAR-MISS, LOGGED: FedWatch printed 64% for a hike by YEAR-END; the fed field's basis is nearest-meeting (Sept 38.1, Day-144 note). A first draft stored the year-end figure and the composite reverted to Disinflation/Hawkish Pivot — a label transition manufactured by a BASIS SWITCH, while the wire actually said hike bets were being pared (DXY down three sessions on it). Draft withdrawn before render, rollback recorded in archive metadata, field basis enforced: Sept 38.1 carried ×4 LOUD; year-end 64 lives in the attestation only. The label holds — honestly — at tenure 5. HOME DEPOT, THE FIRST CONSUMER WITNESS, WAS STEADIER THAN FEARED: beat top and bottom (EPS 4.92 vs 4.73, sales $47.86B, comps +1.7%), guidance reaffirmed, 'smaller projects' — the household's testimony opens neutral-to-firm; Empire State a four-year high, NY Fed services 0.5. Monday's exacts recovered ×9 (Dow 53,459.78, Nasdaq 26,644.91, DXY 99.57 closing the ×2, WTI 84.29). Tomorrow: FOMC minutes, Lowe's, Target, exact Tuesday Dow/Nasdaq, the 30Y's Tuesday print, VIX (×2), BoC.

editions.summary: THE BUYERS' STRIKE MET A PUBLIC BUYER. A day after the 30Y touched its highest since June 2007, the Treasury announced it will MORE THAN DOUBLE its debt buybacks — from $2 billion to 'at least' $4 billion per operation — explicitly targeting the 10-to-20 and 20-to-30 year sectors that have seen a buyers' strike since late June. Yields cratered on the announcement: the 30Y fell 10 basis points to 5.18 in the session, the largest one-day long-end rally of the run — and the DOLLAR FELL TO A THREE-MONTH LOW, the premium changing address rather than disappearing. The A-2 view names it: the intervention caps the yield, it does not remove the premium — and by fighting it, the Treasury confirmed the premium is real. Under the two-track design this is a FISCAL act on the long-end channel, not a war act: HOLD #10 (Trump's 'no ongoing talks, none scheduled' is a declaration, zero). THE MINUTES leaned watchful: support for a potential hike if inflation does not cool — qualitative, Sept 38.1 carried ×5 LOUD. THE CONSUMER CHORUS, DAY TWO: Target beat firmly (sales +5.3%, comps +3.8%, stock +4.3%) while Lowe's guided soft (-2%) — two witnesses firm, one cautious, against Friday's soft macro data; the household is steadier than the sentiment index said. The tape ended a three-day losing streak on the buyback news plus a biotech moonshot (Moderna +177% on melanoma Phase 3 data, Merck +10%+), with chipmakers falling again (Sandisk -9%) — exact closes unprinted at build, zones flagged. Global context sharpened the intervention's logic: Japanese long yields near 40-year highs, German 30Y highest since 2011, the national debt passing $40 trillion TODAY — duration competition everywhere. Monday's back-derivations got a verbatim triple-confirm (7,745.06 / 26,644.91 / 53,459.78). USDJPY corrected to ~159 (intervention giveback; Macquarie: the July 31 US leg was ~$500M — signal, not size). Canada tariffs paused (BoC-relevant). Tenure 6. Tomorrow: exact Wednesday closes, the 30Y's follow-through (does 5.18 hold without the announcement effect?), Walmart — the chorus's biggest witness — plus the 10Y/DXY/gold/VIX refresh queue and the BoC pull.

SIZED +2, NOT +3 (operator S/N ruling): escalation 68 -> 70; resolution 10 -> 9; stalemate 12 -> 11; base 10 held. The cell is already dominant and this is the fourth rule-fire in seven sessions — S/N dynamics argue for the smallest move that keeps the acts/words discipline intact, not a hold that would zero an executed act. The Axios mid-September reopening objective (50 ships nightly, 60-70% of pre-war exports) is a stated target = declaration, ZERO; it scores DOWN only when channel-widening is an executed act. editions.summary: REVISION #20 — THE LONG WEEKEND CROSSED THREE LINES. On Saturday the IRGC fired two ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships, a carrier and a destroyer — the first direct missile attack on American capital ships in this cycle — and the US answered by striking three Iranian oil tankers off Kharg, in the Gulf of Oman and near Jask; Central Command said one sank, the first Iranian state vessel put on the seabed by US action. Iran hit three US-linked tankers and three US-affiliated vessels and on Sunday claimed a strike on an unmanned American ship. On Monday, Iran's Houthi allies struck Saudi Aramco's 400,000-barrel Jizan refinery and facilities at Abha, Khamis Mushait and Najran with drones and ballistic missiles, wounding more than seventy and halting operations at several energy sites — the proxy carried the war onto Gulf oil infrastructure with mass casualties. Three distinct new classes of act; the ledger scores acts when they occur. Escalation 70 to 73, resolution 9 to 8, stalemate 11 to 9, base 10 — sized at three on the operator's signal-to-noise standard: a larger class jump than #19, in a cell already dominant. The words — 'no more proportionate responses,' 'faster, heavier, more painful,' 'destroy and sink,' 'small potatoes' — are zero. Twenty revisions; none on words. THE OIL CLOCK READ FIVE OF FIVE. WTI settled 93.03, a fifth consecutive close above ninety and the highest since June 4; Brent 97.92, its highest since July 23, after touching 98. The escalation cell is now true on every criterion it was written with — strike-exchange days, Hormuz disruption, and the sustained barrel — logged as full-criteria confirmation, not as a separate weight input. Goldman said Brent could exceed 120 in 2027 if Gulf output stays four million barrels a day below prewar. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE FIVE AND FIRMED ON THE BARREL: robustness 0.35 LOW; the Supply leg's boundary distance doubled to 0.152; the Policy leg eased to 0.433 as September hike pricing slipped toward a coin flip ahead of Friday's CPI. Growth held RESILIENT at the line. AND THE HAVENS WENT THE WRONG WAY AGAIN. The Dow fell 628 to 52,786.07, back-to-back losses; the S&P 7,673.52; the Nasdaq 26,421.41. Yet volatility sat near fifteen and three-quarters, gold spot fell 1.7 percent to 4,356 on the most escalatory weekend of the war, and the dollar lost to all seven currencies in the FX layer — the yen at 153.997, down 3.9 percent in five sessions with no intervention confirmed; the offshore yuan at a new 52-week strong extreme of 6.6831. Two-year 4.37, ten-year 4.79, thirty-year 5.25 — steady, armed. Foreign investors, CNBC reports, now favor US equities over Treasurys. The barrel is carrying this label alone. GOVERNANCE: H.15 reference legs posted and applied for Sept 3-4; VIXCLS confirms Sept 1-3 exactly. Sept-8 VIX and DXY are PROVISIONAL — close prints not captured in the pull window; hard stop tomorrow. Brent: 177bp source-basis variance as the front month rolled to November — third I8 crude instance; a single declared Brent basis is now overdue. Friday: CPI. Next week: the FOMC and the BOJ.

editions.summary: REVISION #21 — THE SECOND ESCAPE VALVE SHUT. Two executed acts of a new class, both traceable to the Iran-aligned network, were scored today. On Thursday September 10 Houthi forces seized Yemen's Red Sea port of Mokha at Bab el-Mandeb — the first territorial capture of a Red Sea port this cycle, and the proxy's first physical hold over the second chokepoint; this was missed in the September 10 and 11 sessions and is recorded as a ledger miss. On the same Thursday and again on Sunday, drones launched from an Iraqi province adjacent to Iran struck facilities on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Madinah regions; late Friday the kingdom shut the seven-million-barrel line to Yanbu with no restart timeline. That pipeline carried roughly six million barrels a day of Gulf crude around the strait for six months; Capital Economics puts up to four percent of world supply at risk, and Yanbu's stocks backstop exports for days. A new launch geography and a new target class — the bypass itself. Escalation 73 to 75, resolution 8 to 7, stalemate 9 to 8, base 10 — sized at two on the operator's signal-to-noise standard: two new classes, proxy-executed, in a cell already at 73. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. AND THE WORDS WENT TO ZERO AS SCORED. Oman postponed the Salalah ministerial on Sunday night, on the eve of the meeting, without a new date — Saudi Arabia objected to amendments to the corridor arrangement and Bahrain declined to attend. The zero the ledger assigned on Friday stands. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE NINE, robustness 0.47 MODERATE. The Policy leg stayed saturated on ninety-percent hike pricing; the Risk leg narrowed again toward its edge as volatility rose to 16.72; the Supply leg held with the oil clock at four of five on either crude basis. THE TAPE: the ten-year touched 5.01 percent in the New York morning — the first print above five since October 2023 — and closed 4.99, its highest close since 2007; the two-year 4.68; the thirty-year 5.33. Brent traded above 108 on the Petroline shutdown and settled near 105.66; WTI near 101.75 — both derived from stated moves on the declared basis and carried provisional pending the wire settles. The Dow fell 152 to 52,421.20, the S&P 7,619.98, the Nasdaq 26,186.41; chips led lower on an AI-safety essay. Gold spot fell 1.2 percent. The dollar was bid against all seven pairs — the first clean sweep on a risk-off day this cycle, the dollar trading as a haven for the first time since September 1; USDCAD rose 285 pips, the loonie weakest since September 4 despite oil: a bypass shutdown is a Canada-negative shock through US demand, not a Canada-positive one through the barrel. editions.summary: HELD, on the eve of the Fed. Nothing on September 15 was an executed act of a new class. The president's claim that 'the failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly' was rejected by Tasnim within hours; Riyadh is reported to be trying to raise Hormuz shipments; Aramco has no restart date for the East-West line. Words, zero. The weekend's mined tanker and attacked cargo vessel are the class already scored. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. THE OIL CHANNEL ARMED ON ITS WRITTEN BASIS. WTI settled near 105.4 — a fifth consecutive close above ninety-five — and Brent traded through 109 with Dubai and Oman grades near 128. Three of the four transmission channels are now armed on a sustained basis; the fourth is CPI, a tenth short. THE TEN-YEAR CLOSED ABOVE FIVE PERCENT FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 2007 — 5.01, after 5.03 intraday, the highest since July 2007 — the thirty-year 5.37, the two-year 4.68; September hike pricing near ninety percent. Stocks fell a second day: the Dow 328 to 52,093.11, the S&P 7,585.73, the Nasdaq 25,981.57, the Russell down 0.9. The dollar was bid against all seven pairs for a second consecutive session — 'higher oil, higher US yields, weaker risk appetite lifted the dollar broadly' — and the Dollar leg's boundary distance collapsed from 0.22 to 0.073 toward its strong edge: the FX layer's regime change is holding. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE TEN, ROBUSTNESS 0.50 MODERATE. The reading enters the Fed's decision with every channel it has armed except the index, the policy leg saturated, and the risk and dollar legs both a tick from confirming. GOVERNANCE — TWO THINGS TO PUT IN FRONT OF THE OPERATOR. First, the base weight has sat at 10 for ten editions and the anchor check fired, as designed. The RegimeStrip build had no path to clear it — the dormant regression flagged on September 2 went live tonight — so the §5 reconfirmation amendment was ported verbatim from the frozen v6.1a, determinism proven byte-identical, and the base reconfirmed under the standing signal-to-noise delegation: nothing in the window bears on the base cell, and moving it to clear a flag is motion without information. Second, all three September 14 hard stops discharged — the derived crude settles were within 36 cents, the carried dollar index was 31 basis points low, and the Cboe 4:00 print was 38 basis points below the official close: that source is retired. Tomorrow: the Fed, the wire settles, the CAD prints, and VIXCLS. Friday: the BOJ.

editions.summary: THE INSTITUTION SIGNED THE HAWKISH HALF. The Federal Open Market Committee raised the funds rate 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00 percent, unanimously, the first increase since 2023; the projections show a median of one more hike this year, with sixteen of eighteen participants expecting at least one and four expecting two. Chairman Warsh: inflation has been too high for too long; the Fed's own test — that underlying inflation is clearly moving to target at sufficient speed — has not been met; the labor market is strong; Middle East tension contributed; the decision was not driven by markets; he is not in the forward guidance business. The Dow gave up more than 600 points during the press conference and closed 631 lower at 51,461.90; the S&P 7,551.81; the Nasdaq flat. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE ELEVEN, robustness 0.50 moderate — and the Dollar leg flipped from neutral to firm. The dollar index closed 100.31, up 0.7 percent, a seven-week high and the first close above 100 since July, after a third consecutive session bid against every pair in the layer. That is the second dimension change of this tenure, following Growth on September 4. The Policy leg stayed saturated; the Risk leg sits at 0.044. THE CURVE BEAR-FLATTENED. The two-year rose seven basis points to 4.74 as the front end absorbed the hike; the ten-year closed 5.02, a second consecutive close above five and a nineteen-year high; the thirty-year held 5.37. Two-tens at 28 basis points. Oil eased for the first time in six sessions as the dollar rose — WTI settled 102.43, Brent 105.83 — and gold spot fell 0.7 percent to 4,264; the VIX closed 17.71, putting the Risk leg back on the line. Bahrain and Oman raised rates with the Fed; Kuwait held. HELD. Nothing in the conflict was an executed act of a new class; the FOMC is a policy act and belongs to the Policy leg, not the ledger. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. GOVERNANCE: the FX market-data tool failed on the first pass and the operator ordered a second; it was restored and all seven pairs were reconciled on the declared basis, along with the wire crude settles, spot gold, the Russell close and the 4:15 VIX — thirteen provisionals reduced to one, and that one corroborated to the cent by recomputing the dollar basket from the confirmed pairs. September 15's four hard stops discharged: the wire settles were 45 cents above the provisional rows, the dollar index 9 basis points below, the VIX 10 basis points above. The container reset at the start of the session; the environment was restored from the r73 bundle and the archive hash verified against the last presented copy. Tomorrow: the seven pairs, the settles, VIXCLS, Bank of Canada. Friday: the BOJ, expected to hike.

editions.summary: HELD. Nothing on September 18 was an executed act of a new class. The State Department approved a 24.3 billion dollar sale of forty-eight F-35s to Saudi Arabia, pending Congress — an arms approval, not a kinetic act, logged at zero. Saudi restoration of the East-West line remains statements; the president meets Gulf leaders next week. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. THE YEN DID THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT A HIKE IS FOR. The dollar bought about 156.25 yen before the decision and 158 by late morning London as traders seized on the two dissents for patience; then, in New York, it snapped back below 157 on what traders described as likely intervention. The Ministry of Finance has not confirmed. The bar closed 156.895. The intervention gauge reads suspected intervention for the first time since the July-August program that spent a record fifteen trillion yen. THE FRONT END MADE A NEW HIGH. The two-year settled 4.741, a fifty-two-week high, up fifty-seven basis points in little more than a month; the ten-year 4.995 after holding near five most of the day; the thirty-year 5.327. Two-tens at 25, its narrowest since March 2025 on Thursday. Markets price a ninety-percent chance of a further hike by December 9, fifty-five for October 28. The label held at tenure thirteen, robustness 0.50 moderate; the Dollar leg held firm; every channel stayed armed. THE TAPE WAS MIXED INTO EXPIRY: the S&P up 0.16 percent to 7,650.07 and down 0.1 on the week; the Nasdaq up 0.39, up 0.7 on the week; the Dow off 97, down 1.7 on the week; the Russell off half a percent. Transports, small caps, industrials and consumer discretionary are down five consecutive weeks; equity funds saw a fourth week of outflows, 31 billion; active-manager exposure fell below 75 from above 100. Oil fell a fourth day — WTI 100.30, Brent 103.87, the week down 1.6 percent — still five dollars above the threshold, with US diesel at a record 6.29. The dollar was softer against six of seven pairs on bar closes, the yen the exception. GOVERNANCE: the first full-layer pull under runbook v1.2 — connector bound, seven pairs on daily-bar closes, paced, gold after the minute — with one wrinkle: the usage endpoint errored while the data path worked, so the preflight rule is amended to use a one-credit data call. editions.summary: HELD. Nothing over the weekend or on September 21 was an executed act of a new class. Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday; the president said he would be open to meeting President Pezeshkian, who is expected in New York for the General Assembly this week; the market hoped for a partial recovery in Saudi shipments, not yet confirmed as flows. Chicago's Goolsbee said inflation may now be demand-driven as well as shock-driven and could require a faster pace of hikes — a Fed official's words. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. OIL BROKE TOWARD THE LINE. WTI spot closed 96.97, a dollar ninety-seven above the ninety-five-dollar channel; the expiring October future settled 95.78, down 4.5 percent, its lowest in more than two weeks; Brent 100.34. The move was priced on diplomacy that has not happened and shipments that have not moved. The sustained-basis clock still reads armed; a close below ninety-five tomorrow starts the disarm question. The strategic reserve stands at 284.6 million barrels, its lowest since 1982. THE TAPE BOUGHT IT. The S&P rose 1.49 percent to 7,764.37 with no intraday pullback, within a percent of its all-time high; the Nasdaq 2.26 percent to 27,122.09; the Dow 368 to 52,050.17; the Russell half a percent — chips and software rallying together, energy the only sector lower. The ten-year fell three basis points to 4.962; the thirty-year 5.29; the two-year 4.756 after a two-year-plus high intraday. Two-tens at 21 basis points, the narrowest since March 2025. The dollar index rose to 100.44, a six-week high, stronger against six of seven pairs on bar closes; Friday's yen snapback faded to 157.39 with Tokyo still silent. Gold spot fell 0.8 percent. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE FOURTEEN, robustness 0.50 moderate — but the Supply leg's margin nearly halved as the barrel fell toward its line. The Dollar leg held firm. Every channel is still armed; one of them is now two dollars from not being. GOVERNANCE: September 18 fully sourced — VIXCLS 14.81 against a 15.44 carry, DXY 100.24 wire-implied. The September 21 VIX carries provisional pending the official print later this morning. Tomorrow: the barrel against ninety-five; Pezeshkian in New York; Thursday the Trump-Xi summit.

editions.summary: HELD — AND THE LONG BOND MADE A TWENTY-TWO-YEAR HIGH. Nothing on September 24 was an executed act of a new class. One act of an existing class was captured late: a commercial vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and one Indian crew member was killed — the class already embodied in the ninety-seven-percent chokepoint condition and the seventy-five-percent escalation cell. No revision; it is logged as a ledger miss, the second of the series after Mokha. An adviser to Iran's supreme leader warned that Iran and the Houthis could open a new front against Red Sea energy supplies — words. Iran's seven-day reopening offer is three days old with no ships under it. The president and Xi extended the trade truce by two months past November 10 — China wanted 2029 — a trade act, not a conflict act. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. THE THIRTY-YEAR CLOSED 5.476 — its highest since 2004 — after printing 5.4461 intraday and rising further into the late session; the ten-year 5.192, the seven-year auction 5.116 and the five-year 5.052 all new fifty-two-week highs; the two-year 4.918. The Treasury bought back six billion of twenty- to thirty-year paper into the move. October hike pricing sits at 66 to 71 percent from 53 before Wednesday's PMI. The curve re-steepened to 27 basis points from the long end — the first bear-steepening of the tenure, and the signature of a market pricing term premium rather than the next hike alone. OIL CAME BACK TOWARD A HUNDRED ON THE PHYSICAL PRICE. [REBASED under ADR-0009:] spot WTI is estimated near 99.85 — the November future settled 94.61, up 2.66 percent on the strait strike and the Red Sea warning, and spot runs five dollars over it in a steeply backwardated curve. The tape was flat: the S&P off two points at 7,704.45, the Dow down 162, the Nasdaq up three, the Russell down three; Fear and Greed 35. The dollar swept all seven pairs a second day, the index near 101.2; the yen closed 158.86 after 159.03 — the 160 line the summer program defended is within a figure and Tokyo has said nothing since the eighteenth; the loonie is at its weakest since August for a fourth day. Gold spot slipped 0.3 percent. New home sales rose 6.4 percent; claims 197 thousand. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE SEVENTEEN, robustness 0.50 moderate. The Supply leg's margin 0.492 on spot; the Dollar leg firmed to 0.302; the Policy leg stayed saturated. Three of four channels armed; the long-end channel is armed at a level not seen since the reading's threshold was written. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. THE THIRTY-YEAR CLOSED 5.50 — through five and a half for the first time since 2004, in what Bloomberg called a vacuum after the sentiment gauge: Michigan's final September reading fell to 48.1, a four-month low, with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6 percent. The ten-year 5.17, the two-year 4.87; two-tens at 30 basis points, the third consecutive day of bear-steepening. Term premium is now the tenure's dominant rate signal. And the equity market shrugged: the Dow rose 479 to 51,828.59, the S&P 0.51 percent to 7,743.50, the Nasdaq 0.48 percent — the S&P roughly flat on a week in which the long bond rose twenty basis points. OIL FELL A FOURTH DAY ON THE FUTURES — AND STAYED ABOVE THE LINE ON THE PHYSICAL PRICE. [REBASED under ADR-0009:] the November future settled 92.41, down 2.33 percent, the week down 3.5 percent; spot is estimated near 97.66, two dollars sixty-six above ninety-five; Brent 104.32. The yen rallied a full percent to 157.30 from 158.86, touching 156.996, with no statement from Tokyo — a move of that shape off 159 is what intervention looks like, and the gauge is on watch. The dollar was softer against four of seven pairs; the two-day sweep broke; the index 101.05. Gold spot rose 0.3 percent. Durable goods were flat against a decline expected. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE EIGHTEEN, robustness 0.50 moderate. The Dollar leg eased to 0.262; the Policy leg stayed saturated; Growth held. Three of four channels armed — the long end at a level the threshold's authors did not anticipate, the strait unchanged, the barrel above its line on the price that matters. editions.summary: HELD — AND THE DOOR THE MARKET PRICED LAST WEEK WAS SHUT WITH WORDS. Nothing over the weekend or on September 28 was an executed act of a new class. The president rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and, according to reports, told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms; in the same breath he said more talks come this week and signalled sanctions relief in exchange for nuclear concessions, and Al Hadath reported Iran had agreed to suspend enrichment — unconfirmed. Fed Governor Cook said AI investment and oil will keep pushing inflation up. Every item is a declaration. Weights 10/8/75/7. Twenty-one revisions; none on words. The governance anchor check fired on the stalemate, escalation and resolution cells — unchanged ten editions since revision 21 — and all three are reconfirmed under the standing delegation: the window held two repeat-class acts and a run of declarations, and no executed act of a new class. Ratification is requested. THE GREAT BOND SELLOFF OF 2026 CONTINUED. The ten-year closed 5.24 after 5.272 intraday, its highest since June 2007; the thirty-year 5.56, highest since 2004; the two-year 4.93; two-tens at 31 basis points, the fourth day of bear-steepening. Gold fell four percent on the spot to a seven-week low as yields and the dollar rose; silver nearly five. Stocks fell — the S&P 0.77 percent to 7,683.69, the Dow 347, the Nasdaq 0.92 percent, the Russell 0.69 — and the breadth beneath was the worst of the tenure: 461 new fifty-two-week lows on the Nasdaq against 50 new highs, 422 against 16 on the NYSE, more than sixty-five percent of issues down. The VIX rose eight percent to 16.07. The dollar was stronger against five of seven pairs, the index near 101.1; the yen held Friday's rally at 157.38 with Tokyo still silent; the loonie at its weakest since August for a sixth day. THIS IS THE FIRST EDITION BUILT ON THE SPOT OIL BASIS. WTI spot is estimated near 97.84 — the November future settled 92.60, up nineteen cents, and spot runs about five dollars over it in a backwardated curve; the estimate is provisional until the EIA posts on Wednesday. The channel is armed; Brent 105.28. The Supply leg's margin 0.392; the Dollar leg 0.277; the Policy leg saturated; Growth resilient. Three of four channels armed. The label held at tenure nineteen, robustness 0.50 moderate. GOVERNANCE: the H.15 release for September 28 reconciled the 24th and 25th — the late-session wire prints overshot the official series by one to two basis points, and the runbook now prefers the four-o'clock wire table. FRED has not updated any series since September 23; the official VIX and EIA spot for six sessions are owed and are being taken from primary sites where they exist. Tomorrow: talks or no talks; the barrel on the physical price; PCE Thursday, payrolls Friday, quarter-end Wednesday.

editions.summary: REVISION #22 — THE FIRST EXECUTED ACT IN TEN SESSIONS, AND IT WAS A PIPELINE. Saudi Aramco restored roughly half the capacity of the East-West line after the September drone strikes, according to Rigzone and Bloomberg; Gulf crude exports reached 12.8 million barrels a day in September, the highest since February, through the bypass and ship-to-ship transfers. On September 17 the kingdom said half the flow would return within days and the ledger scored it at zero; today it is executed and it scores. An act that restores capacity around the chokepoint lowers the chokepoint's marginal leverage without ending the conflict: escalation 75 to 73, stalemate 8 to 9, resolution 7 to 8, base unchanged at 10. Twenty-two revisions; none on words. Everything else was words: the president rejected Iran's full-traffic proposal and said he had offered Iran nothing; Qatar's mediation reported minimal progress; Iranian officials privately doubt a deal before the midterms. The SPR's forty-million-barrel exchange is the final tranche of an existing pledge; the RBA's hike is a third-party policy act. THE OIL CHANNEL WENT OFF — ON AN ESTIMATE. November WTI settled 89.38, down 3.5 percent, on the SPR tranche and the Saudi relief. The spot estimator adopted under ADR-0009 adds the last posted differential of 5.24 and prints 94.62, thirty-eight cents below the line, and the engine's transmission state moved to partial activation, two of four. The rule is reported as it produces the state, flagged provisional on every surface: EIA's physical print comes tomorrow with data through Monday, and a same-day differential of 5.62 or more — inside the observed range — keeps the channel armed. Brent's November contract settled 102.59; December, already the active month at 96.16, becomes the front month tomorrow, a six-dollar roll that will be annotated and not chained. THE CURVE STEEPENED A FIFTH DAY. The thirty-year 5.61, a twenty-year high; the ten-year 5.282; the two-year 4.934; two-tens 35. The Conference Board consumer index fell to 81.9, the lowest in more than twelve years, against October hike pricing of 68 percent and December of 95 — the Fed priced to tighten into the weakest consumer reading since 2014. Stocks did little in a tight range; the dollar swept six of seven pairs, the euro at a three-month low, the loonie at its weakest since August for a seventh day; gold bounced 1.6 percent off a seven-week low. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE TWENTY, robustness 0.50 moderate; the Supply leg's margin narrowed to 0.23 on the estimate; the Dollar leg firmed. Two of four channels armed — the long end and the strait — with the strait's own figure a September 2 vessel-count vintage that flow data says is now stale; a PortWatch refresh is opened as an owed item. GOVERNANCE: the official series remain frozen — FRED has not updated the VIX, Treasury or spot-oil series since September 23 — so six fields carry pending; EIA's own release is tomorrow. Revision #22 is made under the S/N delegation and ratification is requested. Tomorrow: EIA's spot print and the oil channel; the Brent roll; whether a bypass at half capacity moves the strait's price.

editions.summary: HELD — AND THE QUARTER CLOSED WITH THE TEN-YEAR AT A 2002 HIGH. Nothing on September 30 was an executed act of a new class. Iran is reviewing the US ceasefire counterproposal with the strait's terms unclear; the Revolutionary Guard said it has been hitting small ships and preventing passage for a long time; the president called the talks very productive. Words. One act of an existing class was captured late: the September 28 strike on the Kuwaiti supertanker Al Funtas — the shipping class already in the ledger, logged as the third miss of the series. Weights 10/9/73/8. Twenty-two revisions; none on words. The base anchor fired at ten editions and is reconfirmed at 10 under the delegation; ratification is requested. THE OFFICIAL SERIES CAME BACK, AND THEY MOVED TWO EDITIONS. After six days frozen, FRED posted EIA's physical oil through September 29 and the Treasury and VIX series through the 28th. The physical price was 93.38 on September 23 — below the line, so Edition 86 is re-issued with the channel off that day — and 96.16 on September 29, above it, so Edition 90 is re-issued with the channel armed, as that edition said it might be. The spot estimator adopted under ADR-0009 missed by four dollars high on the 23rd and 24th and a dollar and a half low on the 28th and 29th; it is now refreshed to the posted differential of 6.78. EIA's September 25 print of 85.23 — seven dollars under the future and fourteen under the next day — is held as a disputed outlier rather than applied. Today's estimate is 97.20, armed, provisional. Brent's November contract expired at 103.53; December at roughly 97.68 becomes front month tomorrow, a six-dollar roll annotated and not chained. THE CURVE STEEPENED A SIXTH DAY INTO QUARTER END. The ten-year closed 5.30, its highest since May 2002; the thirty-year 5.65, a twenty-year high; two-tens 40 basis points — and this on a day core PCE cooled to 3.0 percent against 3.3 expected and ADP beat at 90 thousand. The long end is not trading inflation prints. Stocks held positive most of the day and rolled over in the final minutes: the S&P off a quarter percent to 7,652.39, down 0.4 for September and up 2.0 for the quarter; the Dow off 441, down 4.3 for the month; the Nasdaq up a quarter percent, the only index up in September, with technology the only positive sector. The dollar was stronger against five of seven pairs; the loonie closed through 1.42 for the first time since August; the Australian dollar at a series low. Gold spot fell 0.6 percent. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE TWENTY-ONE, robustness 0.50 moderate. Three of four channels armed. The strait's figure is refreshed to 98.8 percent on the declared PortWatch vessel basis — one transit on September 27 against a baseline of eighty-five a day — while Kpler's barrel count has flows at roughly half of pre-war, which would read 51 percent and sit below the threshold. The two bases disagree the way futures and spot disagreed on oil, and the decision between them is the operator's. GOVERNANCE: a six-day publication stall resolved in one pass; two editions re-issued on the official physical price; the estimator's error documented; one official print disputed; the Hormuz basis question opened. Tomorrow: the Brent roll; October 1 and whatever Washington's funding deadline produced; the first day of the quarter on a curve at 2002 levels.

editions.summary: REVISION TWENTY-THREE — ON A SHIP ORDER, NOT A STRIKE. The United States ordered a third carrier strike group to the region: the Theodore Roosevelt, with the Makin Island amphibious group, roughly nine thousand personnel, arriving by the end of October. The president said new strikes on Iran are possible after November 3. The ledger scores acts, and a deployment order is one — orders issued, ships moving — of a class the series had not scored before: it has moved on strikes, missiles, tankers, seizures, closures, sanctions, cessations and restorations, never on a posture surge. It moves on this one at the posture weight, two points, not the four a kinetic act would carry: escalation 73 to 75, stalemate 9 to 8, resolution 8 to 7, base anchored at 10 as reconfirmed yesterday. Twenty-six escalation acts on the ledger. Ratification is requested under the delegation. SCORED ZERO: the FlyDubai cockpit altercation of September 30, diverted to Tabuk — the president's 'yes' when asked about Iranian involvement is an attribution claim no carrier or authority has confirmed; the Iranian president's 'ready for negotiations'; and reports that Chinese refiners have suspended October fuel exports, unverified and a supply watch item rather than a scenario act. THE FRONT END RALLIED AND THE LONG END STAYED. ISM manufacturing missed at 54.5 against 55 expected, but its prices-paid index printed 77.9 against 72.3 — the second-highest reading of the cycle. The two-year fell eight basis points to 4.80; the ten-year touched 5.34 intraday, its highest since April 2002, and closed 5.24; the thirty-year held 5.66. Two-year to thirty-year, 86 basis points. A growth miss bought the front end a rally and the long end declined to join it: the term-premium reading of the last six sessions survived its first test. Stocks were flat to firm — the S&P up 0.18 percent to 7,666.45, the Russell up a third of a percent. The dollar index closed 102.10; the euro at a seventeen-month low; the yen through 158; the Australian dollar at another series low; the loonie the only pair to firm. Gold spot rose half a percent. OIL ROSE TO NINETY CENTS FROM THE LINE. November WTI settled 92.87, up 2.7 percent, and Brent's new December front month 102.31, up 4.4 percent — the November Brent contract expired yesterday at 103.53, a roll annotated and not chained. The fair-value spot for the day is a provisional 94.10: the exchange's final settlements post tomorrow morning and the connector's curve returned yesterday's snapshot again, so December is carried at yesterday's final spread. From today the engine reads that same-day fair value — the operator's instruction is that the reference carry no days-old levels — and the three-session median adopted last night is retired. Days 171 to 179 are re-based on the same-day basis: the energy leg was off on September 22, on on the 24th and off again on the 29th; no label or tag moved; six editions are re-issued. Today the channel is off by ninety cents, and a December settle a dollar wider than carried would switch it on. RECONCILIATION CLOSED THE QUARTER'S BOOKS. The Federal Reserve's H.15 for September 29 and 30 is applied — the ten-year's quarter-end close is 5.29 on the official series; the September 30 VIX is 16.34, not the 16.04 carried; the September 30 fair-value spot finalises at 91.71 on the official December settle; a Toronto index carry that had gone stale since September 28 is corrected. Labels and tags did not move. One erratum: yesterday's edition pointed to an October 1 funding deadline that did not exist — the continuing resolution signed September 2 runs to December 11. THE LABEL HELD AT TENURE TWENTY-TWO. Two of four channels armed: the long end and the strait, the latter still on the declared vessel basis with the barrel-basis question open for the operator. Tomorrow: the September payrolls, the CME print that finalises today's oil reference, and whether a third carrier's departure is followed by anything else that moves.

editions.summary: THE GROWTH LEG TURNED, AND THE LABEL DID NOT. September payrolls rose 29 thousand against 90 expected; August was revised down to 133; the two prior months lost 60 thousand between them; unemployment rose to 4.2 percent; average hourly earnings rose a tenth. The Growth Signal moved from resilient to slowing — the first dimension to change in twenty-three sessions — and the composite held, because cost-push inflation, a hawkish central bank and a softening economy is precisely the configuration Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot names. Robustness rose to 0.56: the growth leg had sat on its boundary for weeks and has now stepped off it, the wrong way. THE FRONT END ROSE ON THE MISS. The two-year closed 4.84, six basis points higher than the official Thursday close; the ten-year 5.28, four higher; the thirty-year 5.61, flat. An October hike repriced to roughly one in four; December stayed priced. A market that lifts the two-year on a weak payroll is a market that thinks the Fed's problem is prices, not jobs — and that is the hawkish-pivot leg speaking. Stocks rallied on the slower hiking path: the S&P up three quarters of a percent to 7,722.85, the Nasdaq-100 at a record, the Russell up nearly a percent; for the week the S&P lost 0.3 and the Dow 1.3. The dollar weakened against six of seven pairs; the loonie was the exception, its tenth day above 1.42 as oil fell. Gold lost 0.9 percent; the VIX 15.31. HELD, BY RULE. A Houthi ballistic missile at Khamis Mushait was intercepted — Houthi-on-Saudi is a class already in the ledger, which now reads 27 escalation acts. Explosions in Sanaa overnight are reported by Houthi media as Saudi strikes and by Yemen's government as twenty of them; Riyadh has not confirmed. If it did, a Gulf state conducting kinetic action in Yemen would be a new class; today it is zero. The G7 and the International Energy Agency agreed a coordinated release of 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over several months — an executed act, and the one that moved oil — but it acts on the transmission channel, not on the conflict path the cells describe; it is scored zero on the weights and the question of whether supply-mitigation acts belong in the matrix is referred to the operator. The president's 'they'll be hit, very hard' and the ambassador's 60-percent enrichment charge are words. 10/8/75/7 stands. OIL FELL UNDER THE RELEASE. November WTI settled 91.11, down 1.9 percent, reversing Thursday's rise; Brent's December held 102.25; the spread between them is eleven dollars. The fair-value spot is a provisional 92.29 — the connector that supplies the second month was unreachable tonight, so December is carried at Thursday's final spread, and no plausible settle brings the day within two dollars of the line. The channel is off by 2.71. RECONCILIATION AND AN ERRATUM. The official series closed Thursday's books: H.15 has the two-year at 4.78 and the thirty-year at 5.61, not the 5.66 two wires printed and this desk carried. Thursday's edition said the long end held while the front end rallied; on the official numbers the long end followed, at a third of the pace. Edition 92 is re-issued with the view restated, and TradingEconomics closes now outrank the wires for the thirty-year. The exchange's final December settle finalised Thursday's fair value at 94.11. TENURE TWENTY-THREE, two of four channels armed. Next: the CME print for today's oil reference; Monday's H.15; whether Riyadh confirms Sanaa; and the first full week with a slowing growth leg under a label built for one.

editions.summary: THE LONG END MADE A NEW HIGH ON THE FIRST DAY OF A SLOWING GROWTH LEG. The ten-year closed 5.31 percent, its highest since 2002 — above the quarter-end 5.29 on the official series — one trading day after a 29-thousand payroll moved the growth leg to slowing. The two-year eased two basis points; the thirty-year rose five to 5.67; two-year to thirty-year, 85. ISM services held at 54.9 with prices paid rising to 74. A curve that steepens from the back on soft growth and firm prices is the term-premium reading at its clearest, and it is now the label's whole rates case: inflation sticky, policy hawkish, growth slowing, the long end pricing supply. Stocks rose regardless — the S&P up two thirds of a percent to 7,774.24, the Nasdaq up one — on the same slower-hike path that lifted them Friday. The dollar was stronger against five of seven; the euro set a new seventeen-month low at 1.1220; the loonie spent an eleventh day above 1.42. HELD, BY RULE, AT A WAR-HIGH TEMPO. Three tankers were struck in the strait on Saturday — one with an engine-room fire, two hit on the port quarter and left without propulsion, per Central Command's maritime centre — and a brand-new LR2, the Lipsi, on Sunday; Iranian strikes are described as at their highest level since the war began, seven 'violating' oilers in five days. The Houthis claimed a strike on an Aramco facility in Riyadh in retaliation for Saudi attacks. Every one of these is a class the ledger has already scored, which now reads thirty escalation acts; none is a new class, so the weights do not move — the rule that built the 75 percent cell is the rule that holds it. Scored zero: Speaker Qalibaf's statement that the strait stays shut until seven conditions of the June memorandum are met; Yemen's announced 'major campaign' against the Houthis with Saudi coalition support, which is a declaration until Riyadh executes and confirms — the day it does, Gulf-state kinetic action in Yemen is a new class; the Camp David deliberations; and the Pentagon's withdrawal of its B-1s from Fairford on plot threats, a defensive relocation that is logged and not scored. 10/8/75/7 stands. OIL FELL A THIRD DAY INTO THE ATTACKS. November WTI settled 89.43, down 1.8 percent; Brent's December 100.32, down 1.9. The fair-value spot is a provisional 90.24 — the only settle print available at the pull was the wire's, flagged as a single source, and December is carried at Friday's final spread; the exchange's print tomorrow governs. The channel is off by 4.76, and no plausible December settle changes that. The reason oil falls while tankers burn is the other half of the strait story: Gulf tanker flows are reported above twelve million barrels a day, near pre-war volumes, which on a barrel basis is a strait about forty percent disrupted — against the declared vessel count, still at 98.8 percent on the latest PortWatch vintage. The desk's basis decision stands and the ten-edition divergence clock starts today. RECONCILIATION. Friday's books closed on the official series: two-year 4.83, ten-year 5.28, thirty-year 5.63 — the wires printed 5.61 and 5.64 either side of it, so no wire is trusted on the thirty-year; the exchange's December settle came in 35 cents under the carried value as the spread narrowed, and Friday's fair value finalised at 92.09. No label or tag moved. TENURE TWENTY-FOUR, two of four channels armed. Tomorrow: the official yields for a ten-year at 5.31; the exchange print for today's oil reference; Riyadh on Sanaa; and whether a barrel-basis strait and a vessel-basis strait can both be true for a tenth edition.

Oil fell a third day as reserve releases and higher Gulf flows outweighed the attacks; the energy condition stays off. Reading held, twenty-fourth day.

editions.summary: THE NEW LABEL'S FIRST FULL SESSION — AND THE FIRST EDITION BUILT ON A FINAL OIL PRINT. The exchange's October 7 settlements — November 88.28, December 87.55 — give a same-day fair-value spot of 88.59, and because this edition was built after the one-o'clock window the engine's oil field is final, not carried: no provisional oil input, no re-issue owed. Supply Shock reads easing by a clear margin and Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot holds at tenure two. The rates leg did the work: the ten-year printed 5.36 intraday, its highest since 2002, closed near 5.30, and a $39 billion auction was taken down at 5.30 against 5.317 when-issued with a 2.77 cover — demand at a twenty-four-year high in yield is not a market fleeing duration, it is a market being paid for it. The two-year eased to 4.77; the thirty-year held 5.68; two-year to thirty-year, 91. THE MINUTES PUT THE HAWKISH LEG ON THE RECORD. September's quarter-point hike was unanimous. Some participants saw it as necessary to offset energy and other price shocks; the committee was split on whether it was precautionary or the start of a materially tighter path. The next meeting is October 27-28. That is the policy dimension of the label in the Fed's own words — a central bank hiking into an oil shock it does not control, now with the oil shock fading on its own measure and growth slowing. Stocks snapped five-day streaks: the S&P off 0.22 percent to 7,802.11, the Dow off 342, the Russell off 1.3; the Nasdaq eased from a record. Gold spot fell 1.65 percent to a two-month low. The dollar was stronger against six of seven; the euro set a third seventeen-month low in a week at 1.1195; the loonie spent a thirteenth day above 1.42. HELD, BY RULE, AT HIGH INTENSITY. Houthi drones and missiles struck Abha and King Khalid airports — three dead, thirty-six injured by Saudi count, the Houthis claiming the attack — Houthi-on-Saudi, a class in the ledger since July. A tanker was hit by multiple projectiles fifty-one miles off Qatar with casualties; UKMTO did not attribute it; the shipping-attack class. The coalition struck eighty-two targets across Saada, Hodeidah, Al-Jawf and Marib, the continuation of the campaign scored yesterday. And Iran's foreign ministry announced that Tehran and Muscat have agreed the coordinates of safe transit routes through the strait, to be communicated to an international maritime body — the class of the August 26 Iran-Oman arrangement, announced and not executed: no coordinates published, no transit under them, and the speaker's seven conditions still standing. Thirty-three escalation acts and seven de-escalation acts on the ledger; none of a new class; 10/8/75/7 stands. RECONCILIATION. Monday's books closed on H.15 — 4.79, 5.27, 5.64, with TradingEconomics two basis points high across the curve — and VIXCLS 15.01; today's VIX of 15.08 was already official at the pull. The thirty-year wires still bracket the official print and are not trusted. TENURE TWO, two of four channels armed. Tomorrow: the official yields for a 5.36 intraday; whether the strait's coordinates become a transit; and whether a label carried by rates alone survives its first week.

editions.summary: THE LABEL REVERTS. November WTI settled 91.49, up 3.6 percent — on reports that Washington was weighing large military operations in Iran before the midterms, on more shipping attacks in the strait and Houthi missiles at Riyadh, and on a hurricane that shut roughly sixty-three percent of US Gulf of Mexico output — and pared its gains after the president wrote that there would be no attack before November 3. The same-day fair-value reference is 91.77, provisional on the second month carried at Wednesday's final spread, but the state is not in doubt: no spread brings the reference under 90, and the Supply Shock rule reads persistent again. The composite returns to Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot after two sessions as Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot — a round trip inside three sessions on a rule with no buffer at a round number. This edition says so plainly: the engine is deterministic, the record is honest, and the observation logged on October 6 that the supply rule has no hysteresis is now evidenced and referred to the engine review. WASHINGTON DECLARED A PAUSE. On Truth Social the president wrote that the United States is 'having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran' and 'will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held ... on November 3rd.' By the hierarchy this is a declaration: the ledger scored an executed cancellation of planned strikes in August, but a pledge not to act is not an act, and Tehran's latest offer was rejected the same week. It is scored zero and logged as a watch window — the first explicit calendar bound on US action in the episode. Houthi ballistic missiles at Riyadh were intercepted, with the Houthi spokesman claiming a hit on King Khalid airport and warning Saudi oil-facility staff to leave — the Houthi-on-Saudi class, thirty-four escalation acts on the ledger. Turkey's foreign minister said the Mecca pact is 'not an offensive agreement' and ruled out troops. 10/8/75/7 stands. RATES EASED FROM THE HIGH AS GILTS MADE THEIRS. The ten-year closed 5.24, down four basis points after a 5.35 intraday print; the thirty-year 5.61, down six; the two-year 4.76. Across the Atlantic the thirty-year gilt touched 6.05 percent, its highest since 1998, and the ten-year 5.53 — the long-end repricing is global, which is the strongest evidence yet that it is term premium and not a US oil story. Claims printed 197 thousand against 200. Stocks split: the S&P off 0.47 percent to 7,765.82, the Nasdaq off 1.25 with health care down nearly two percent and energy up 2.6; the Dow and Russell flat. Gold spot rose 0.8 percent. The dollar weakened against six of seven; the loonie firmed with oil, a fourteenth day above 1.42. RECONCILIATION. Wednesday's books closed on H.15 — 4.77, 5.28, 5.67. This edition was built at the operator's request before the one-o'clock window, so tonight's oil level is owed to the exchange's final at the next build; the state is not. TENURE ONE, again; two of four channels armed. Tomorrow: the exchange's print; the official yields; whether a declared pause changes the tempo in the strait; and whether this label holds a session longer than the last one did.

editions.summary: HELD, AND THE SURVEY DATA AGREED WITH THE LABEL. Michigan's preliminary October sentiment fell to 46.3 against 47.8 expected — current conditions 44.7 against 51 — while one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7 percent and five-year to 3.5. Soft activity and rising price expectations in a single release is Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot in survey form, and the curve read it that way: the two-year rose five basis points to 4.80 against the official Thursday close, the ten-year two to 5.24, the thirty-year held 5.60 — a bear-flattening on an inflation-expectations print, with growth slowing. Stocks looked through it to the week: the Dow up 0.83 percent to 51,660 for its best week since early August, the S&P up 0.59 to 7,811.98 and 1.15 on the week, the Nasdaq and Russell higher. Gold spot rose 1.5 percent. The dollar was mixed — firmer against the euro, which lost a fifth straight week, the yen at a series high of 158.25 inside the intervention range, and the loonie, which touched 1.43 intraday; softer against sterling, the Australian dollar, the franc and a yuan at its firmest of the series. editions.summary: REVISION TWENTY-FOUR — ON A MISSILE INTO AN AIRPORT TERMINAL. On Saturday a Houthi ballistic missile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh: thirteen dead, among them a United States citizen, more than three hundred wounded, the airport closed since and its suspension extended today. A second projectile hit the domestic terminal on Sunday and killed one more; King Fahd in Dammam was targeted; the week's toll at Saudi airports is around twenty. The ledger has scored Houthi strikes on Saudi targets since July, and it scored the first shipping attack with fatalities in August as a class of its own — so a mass-casualty strike on Gulf civilian infrastructure, with the first American killed in this episode, is a new class by the record's own precedent, not a heavier instance of an old one. It is scored plus two at the kinetic weight: escalation 75 to 77, stalemate 8 to 7, resolution 7 to 6, base anchored at 10. Forty escalation acts on the ledger. The president said the United States 'may' join Saudi operations against the Houthis — words, but the path this class opens. Ratification is requested under the delegation. SCORED AS REPEAT CLASSES: a US fighter disabled the Panama-flagged Ocean Molica out of an Iranian port on Saturday and the military disabled a second blockade-runner on Sunday — enforcement acts already in the record; the Revolutionary Guard claimed three supertankers struck in two days, the third afire today, with UKMTO silent on the twelfth; airstrikes on two Sanaa districts, attributed by the Houthis to Riyadh and unconfirmed. Words: the energy minister's 'equally serious response', Tehran 'still reviewing' the US answer to its seven-point proposal, Iran blaming Washington and Israel for the shipping disruption. THE DOLLAR MADE AN EIGHTEEN-MONTH HIGH AGAINST EVERYTHING. The index closed 102.59 and the dollar was stronger against all seven pairs: the euro at a new seventeen-month low of 1.1154, the yen at 158.65 — a series high, 1.35 from the level where the Ministry of Finance has acted — the loonie a sixteenth day above 1.42, the yuan giving back Friday's firmness. Oil rose 2.1 percent to 93.74 for November as the airport attacks outweighed Russian diesel; the same-day fair value is 93.96, provisional on the carried second month, one dollar and four cents under the $95 channel — and no plausible December settle arms it tonight. Brent's December closed 106.65, a two-week high. Cleveland's Hammack said the Fed should move 'relatively quickly' to a restrictive stance as inflation broadens — the policy leg in a sentence. HOLIDAY BOOKS. The US cash Treasury market was closed; the two-, ten- and thirty-year are carried at Friday's closes — 4.80, 5.24, 5.60 — and flagged, with no official observation to come for today and Friday's H.15 due Tuesday. Toronto was closed for Thanksgiving. Equities traded flat to down: the S&P off six hundredths to 7,807.64, the Nasdaq off 0.44 percent, the Dow up 0.38. Gold spot fell 0.6 percent; the VIX 15.21. Friday's oil finalised on the exchange's December settle at 92.15. WEDNESDAY IS THE TEST. Consensus has September CPI re-accelerating to 3.6 percent headline, 2.5 core. A print at consensus arms the inflation channel for the first time this tenure and takes transmission to three of four with oil a dollar from making it four. Tenure three. Correction to Edition 98: CPI is Wednesday the 14th, not Tuesday.

editions.summary: SIXTY-SIX CENTS FROM THE THIRD CHANNEL, ON THE EVE OF CPI. November WTI settled 94.14, up forty cents; the same-day fair-value reference is 94.34, provisional on the second month carried at Monday's final spread, and no plausible December settle takes it through $95 tonight — but a November settle above roughly 94.80 tomorrow, at the current spread, arms the oil channel. Consensus has September CPI at 3.6 percent headline against a 3.5 condition and 2.5 core. Wednesday can therefore take transmission from two channels armed to four — long end, strait, oil and inflation — or leave it at two. The long end eased into the print: ten-year 5.22, thirty-year 5.57, two-year 4.79; the dollar gave back Monday's eighteen-month high against all seven pairs; stocks closed flat with the banks mixed — Goldman's equities 'blowout', JPMorgan's FICC miss offset by net-interest guidance, Wells Fargo's 'trading slowed meaningfully' in late September. HELD, BY RULE. A container ship was hit by a projectile in the strait late in the evening, unattributed by UKMTO — the shipping class. Houthi missiles were intercepted near Aramco's Riyadh headquarters and an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was attacked, Saudi Arabia reporting no casualties — the Houthi-on-Saudi energy class, scored since July. Forty-two escalation acts on the ledger. The Houthis declared Aramco's facilities legitimate targets and told workers to leave; the president, after a call with the crown prince, said the Houthis are 'behaving very badly' and that he will 'be there after the midterm elections' — a second declared calendar bound, this one on Yemen; an Iraqi militia threatened US forces if Washington joins. Words, all of them. The United States lifted sanctions on Russian diesel alongside last week's supply arrangement — an executed supply-mitigation act, transmission-only by the operator's rule; diesel futures rose two percent regardless. 10/7/77/6 stands. THE FED SPOKE BOTH LEGS OF THE LABEL IN ONE INTERVIEW. New York's Williams still sees one more hike this year as appropriate and none in 2027, with inflation slowing 'quite a bit' toward target — the hawkish pivot with a declared end-date, which is what a market steepening the curve on supply rather than prints has been saying for three weeks. Existing home sales rose to 3.99 million; small-business optimism slipped to 97.9. RECONCILIATION. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release confirmed Friday's two-, ten- and thirty-year at 4.80, 5.24 and 5.60 — the provisionals to the basis point — and marked Monday 'Markets closed', so the holiday carry closes as the record. Monday's oil finalised at 93.97 on the exchange's December settle, a cent from the provisional. The H.15 release page itself, which returns every maturity in one read with holiday markers, is adopted as the canonical rates fetch; the FRED series pages lag it by hours. The FX connector was absent on the first preflight and bound on the second; the outage is logged. TENURE FOUR, two of four channels armed and two within reach. Tomorrow decides more about this label's transmission than any day since it was named.

editions.summary: FULL TRANSMISSION. September CPI printed 3.7 percent against 3.6 expected and 3.4 in August, up six tenths on the month with gasoline the main driver; core 2.6 against 2.5. The inflation channel armed. November WTI settled 95.09, up 95 cents, and the same-day fair-value reference is 95.28 — provisional on the second month carried at Tuesday's final spread, but robust: a zero spread still reads 95.09, above the line. The oil channel armed. With the thirty-year at 5.53 and the strait at 95.3 percent on the declared basis, all four transmission channels are lit for the first time in this tenure and for the first time since the label was given its name — the frozen engine's own string stops at three, 'multi-channel activation', with the strait the truncated fourth; the surfaces state four of four from the inputs. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot holds at tenure five, inflation leg further from its boundary, every channel the configuration was built to flag now active in the same week the New York Fed described the cycle's last hike. THE MARKET READ IT THE WAY THE LABEL DOES. The two-year rose two basis points to 4.81 on the official Tuesday close and traded above 4.92 intraday as October became, in the wire's phrase, 'a closer call'; the ten-year fell two to 5.19 and the thirty-year three to 5.53 — a bear-flattening, the front end pricing the hike and the long end pricing what the hike does to growth. Stocks sold off: the S&P down 1.1 percent to 7,720.14, the Nasdaq down 1.9 with technology off three, the Russell down 1.9; staples and health care up two. The VIX rose ten percent to 16.87. Gold spot fell 1.5 percent and silver six. The dollar was stronger against all seven pairs, back at its eighteen-month high; the yen traded to 158.96. The thirty-year mortgage reached 7.50 percent, its highest since 2023. Bank of America missed and was fined $1.2 billion; Morgan Stanley and BlackRock beat. HELD, BY RULE. Near the strait one ship was hit by a projectile and another sank after striking a sea mine — the first confirmed mine casualty since the Larak mine-laying was scored in August, a shipping-class act whose intensity is noted; the coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh; the Houthis claimed Tuesday's Dhahran strike and vowed to continue against airports and oil facilities. Forty-five escalation acts on the ledger, none of a new class. Reuters reports Iranian officials saying the strait tactics changed about ten days ago to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterms — an attributed report, not an act; Tehran called the US response on reopening the strait 'insufficient'. 10/7/77/6 stands. The base anchor set on September 30 comes due at Day 188: the engine's check did not flag, and a voluntary review reconfirms base at 10 — no act in the window bears on the normalisation path, and a 3.7 CPI with a hiking Fed moves that path further off, but the cell is at its floor. Ratification is requested. RECONCILIATION. Tuesday's yields finalised on the Fed's H.15 at 4.79, 5.21 and 5.56, within a basis point of the provisionals; Tuesday's oil at 94.36 on the exchange's December settle. Tonight's oil level is owed to the exchange's final; the channel state is not. TENURE FIVE, FOUR OF FOUR. Next: PPI and retail sales tomorrow, the Chair later in the week, the November contract's expiry on Tuesday — and whether a label running on full transmission can hold its energy leg through a roll.

editions.summary: FULL TRANSMISSION, SECOND SESSION — AND DEEPER. September producer prices rose 1.3 percent on the month and 6.3 percent on the year against 5.3 expected; core 5.0 against 4.4. Where Wednesday's CPI could be read as a gasoline month, Thursday's PPI cannot: the pass-through is in the pipeline. November WTI settled 97.97, up 3 percent, on the exchange's final print, and the fair-value reference is 98.21 — three dollars and twenty-one cents over the oil condition, with no carried second month in it. The strait reads 97.6 percent on the declared vessel basis after PortWatch counted two transits a day on October 11 against a baseline of 85; the barrel basis, by TankerTrackers and Kpler, says more than twelve million barrels a day are moving, most under American escort — the two measures now diverge by the widest margin of the series. The thirty-year at 5.41 is still above five. Four of four, held; Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure six. THE CURVE DID THE OPPOSITE OF WEDNESDAY. On the hottest producer-price print of the cycle the whole curve rallied: the two-year fell seven basis points to 4.75, the ten-year eleven to 5.08 — it had traded above 5.32 on Wednesday morning — and the thirty-year eleven to 5.41. October is now priced at 71 percent hold. Equities rose: the Dow up 1.1 percent to 52,184.20, the Russell 1.4, the S&P a third of a percent to 7,745.30, the Nasdaq flat as semiconductors fell a seventh straight session; health care made a record and the energy majors 52-week highs. The VIX closed 16.46 after a two-week high intraday. Gold spot rose 1.8 percent to 4175.13. The dollar weakened against all seven pairs from Wednesday's eighteen-month high; the loonie closed below 1.42 for the first time since mid-September. Retail sales beat on the headline and missed on the control group; the Philadelphia survey's new orders collapsed while New York's jumped; claims 199,000. The market read a 6.3 PPI as margin compression and a demand problem rather than a policy one. editions.summary: OIL THROUGH ONE HUNDRED, PROVISIONALLY — AND THE STRAIT RE-BASED. The wire has rolled to the December contract two sessions before November expires: December settled 99.02, up 2.6 percent, having traded above 101 intraday — the highest close since September 17 — and November was not quoted. The reference is built tonight from December plus Thursday's final November-December spread of 1.47: a constructed front month of 100.49 and a fair-value spot of 100.68. That is provisional in a stronger sense than usual — the front month is not an observed settle — and the exchange's final governs. What is robust is the channel: at any spread, including zero, the reference is at least 99.02. What is not robust is the handle. Brent settled 109.86, up 3.7 percent, its highest since May. Import prices rose 1.1 percent on the month and export prices 2.2 — eight and twelve percent on the year — the day after a 6.3 PPI. The inflation leg has deepened three sessions running. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure seven. THE STRAIT: DE-ANCHORED, BY RULING. The operator ruled tonight that the chokepoint field must not carry a stale count — only the latest measurement. PortWatch's feed, queried directly, shows its last Hormuz observation is October 11: two transits, and a first-half-of-October series that never exceeded eight a day. The engine had been reading that five-day-old count as 97.6 percent disrupted, and its source string still cited October 4 — a defect, logged. Under the new rule the field takes the most recently dated measure in the set: CENTCOM's commander said on October 16 that US forces helped four hundred merchant vessels through the strait in the past week — fifty-seven a day against a baseline of 85, or 32.8 percent disrupted. The tanker trackers' barrel basis, dated the 15th, reads about forty. Every fresh measure puts the strait below the seventy-percent line. The chokepoint channel is off; transmission reads three of four — long end, oil, CPI — which is also, for the first time, exactly what the frozen engine's own string says. The four-of-four readings of Tuesday and Wednesday rested on the October 11 count when it was three and four days old; they are annotated, not re-issued, and a retrospective re-base is offered. This edition is re-issued: the first issue carried 97.6. THE RISK LEG MOVED. The VIX closed 19.99, up 21 percent and its highest since early September. The S&P fell 1.09 percent to 7,660.65 — its first decline of more than one percent in fifty-five sessions, the longest such run in more than six years — and lost 1.95 percent on the week; the Nasdaq fell 2.14 percent to 26,139.94 for a 4.48 percent week, its worst since June, with semiconductors down an eighth straight session; the Russell fell 1.66 percent; the Dow 0.34, up on the week. The curve did not move: thirty-year 5.43 flat, ten-year 5.09, two-year down five basis points to 4.72. The dollar weakened against all seven pairs for a second day; the loonie held below 1.42. Thursday the curve priced a growth problem; Friday equities did. HELD, BY RULE. The Houthis fired two missiles at Aden's airport, claiming a Saudi command centre; the coalition destroyed a ballistic missile aimed at Yanbu, two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones. One act is captured late: on October 6 CENTCOM destroyed an Iranian-linked dhow in the Gulf of Oman it said was spotting for IRGC targeting — the class the blockade already established; the fourth ledger miss of the series. Fifty-one acts. Iran's navy reported a tanker on fire in a prohibited area with its transponder off — unnamed, unscored until identified. Pezeshkian said Iran has 'always been ready for dialogue' and 'will not bow to coercion'; the army said the strait reopens when the United States leaves; CBS reported Pentagon planning for the MOAB against Iranian sites. editions.summary: NOVEMBER'S LAST FULL SESSION, AND THE REFERENCE IS 103.74. The wire quotes November again tonight — the same wire that called Friday's print December — at 103.66, up 2.2 percent, the highest front-month settle since September 15. With one day to expiry the interpolation barely matters: any December spread between zero and three dollars puts the fair-value spot between 103.66 and 103.76. Friday's exchange final also arrived: November 101.41 against December 99.02, a spread of 2.39 rather than the 1.47 carried from Thursday, so Friday's constructed reference was a dollar and four cents low; the correction is applied, the channel was never in question, and the construct procedure keeps its place with a wider error band. The oil channel is armed by nearly nine dollars. The Supply reading is now $6.26 from the $110 line at which PERSISTENT becomes ACUTE — the first time that line has been the nearer one. Brent 109.55. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure eight. THE STRAIT, ON THE LATEST COUNT. Under Friday's rule the chokepoint field takes the most recently dated measure and carries nothing. Tonight that is Kpler's: crude flows through the strait averaged about 8.5 million barrels a day in the week to Monday, down from more than twenty the week before, with at least ten confirmed incidents against commercial vessels. Against the twenty-million baseline that is 57.5 percent disrupted — up from the 32.8 CENTCOM's escorted-transit count gave on Friday, and up from the ~40 the barrel trackers gave a week ago. The chokepoint channel remains off at the seventy-percent line; transmission is three of four. The measure is moving toward the line, not away from it, and it moved twenty-five points in a week. The Revolutionary Guards say a tanker struck a mine in the southern strait on Sunday and exploded; no vessel is named and no monitor has confirmed it — unscored. PortWatch's own feed has not produced a Hormuz observation since October 11. MARKETS. Stocks recovered part of Friday: the S&P rose 0.41 percent to 7,692.02, well off its highs into Tesla and Meta week; the Nasdaq 1.11 percent, as semiconductors ended an eight-session losing streak, the longest since 2010; the Russell a quarter; the Dow flat. The VIX fell to 18.44. The curve gave back: two-year 4.78, ten-year 5.15, thirty-year 5.48 — four to six basis points higher — as the Houthi claims lifted oil and yields together. The NAHB index fell to 29, the lowest since June 2012, with prospective-buyer traffic at 18. The dollar was mixed, weaker against the euro, sterling, the loonie, the Aussie and the yuan, stronger against the yen and the franc; the loonie's third close below 1.42. Gold fell 0.6 percent. The Fed meets next week and is expected to hold. HELD, BY RULE. The Houthis claimed strikes on Aramco's Yanbu facility, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International in Riyadh and Abha airport; Saudi civil defence issued alerts and cleared them, no damage was reported, and Riyadh has not confirmed the targets. The launches are evidenced by the alerts and scored as the existing Houthi-on-Saudi-infrastructure class. Shaybah is flagged: a confirmed hit on an upstream field would be the first of its kind in the series and would be reviewed as a new class. In Shabwa a Houthi strike on a government training camp killed fifty-three — the deadliest single act on the intra-Yemen front since fighting resumed, scored as the Aden-palace class of last Thursday with the intensity noted and referred alongside it. Fifty-five acts. On Friday the president signed an order waiving some sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy exports — an executed act, supply mitigation, transmission only, as the diesel waiver was; analysts said it does little for the physical disruption in the strait. Iran says its conditions for reopening the strait remain on the table; Egypt's parliament deferred its vote on assisting Saudi Arabia to the 26th. Words. 10/7/77/6 stands. RECONCILIATION. Thursday's and Friday's yields are final on H.15; the same-evening read matched the ten- and thirty-year to the basis point. Friday's oil is final at 101.72. Friday's housing starts, permits, consumer sentiment and the Chair's remarks are still owed — a second edition running — and flagged as such. TENURE EIGHT, THREE OF FOUR. Next: the exchange's final tonight; November's expiry tomorrow and the roll to December-January on Wednesday, annotated not chained; whether Kpler's next weekly count carries the strait measure through seventy; and whether Shaybah was hit.
