editions.summary: NOVEMBER EXPIRED AT 101.79, AND FOR ONE NIGHT THE REFERENCE IS EXACT. On its last trading day the November contract settled 101.79, down 1.8 percent; with no days to expiry the fair-value interpolation collapses to the front month, so the reference is the settle, independent of any second-month spread — the only provisionality is the single print, which the exchange's final will confirm overnight. Monday's final also arrived, and it explains the week's construct errors: November settled 103.66 while December fell to 98.54, a spread of $5.12 against the 2.39 carried — the expiring contract ran an expiry squeeze the deferred months did not share. Monday's reference reconciles to 103.83. From Wednesday the engine reads December and January; on Monday's curve that pair would print about 98.7, so the reference steps down roughly three dollars by construction — annotated, not chained — and the channel survives at any December settle above about 93. The Supply reading moves back from the $110 line to $8.21 away. Brent 108.79. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure nine. THE RATE-SENSITIVE ECONOMY IS ROLLING OVER. Housing starts fell 5.9 percent to 1.221 million against 1.305 expected, single-family starts fell 4.8, pending home sales fell 7.3 percent on the month against a flat consensus, and the builders' index yesterday was the lowest since 2012. The curve bear-flattened again — two-year 4.80, thirty-year 5.44 — with the Fed in blackout and a hold expected next week, the wire noting that hotter inflation and higher oil have 'revived concerns about further rate hikes'. Equities rotated defensive: health care at a record, utilities, staples and real estate strong, the Dow up one percent and the Russell 1.65, the Nasdaq flat. The VIX fell to 17.31 and the Risk dimension returned to RISK_ON by the narrowest margin of the series after two sessions in transition. The dollar weakened against all seven pairs; the loonie's fourth close below 1.42; the yen firmer on a record-demand long-bond auction. THE STRAIT AND THE LEDGER. Hormuz stays at 57.5 percent on Kpler's October 19 count, the latest dated measure; nothing newer was published today, and the Revolutionary Guards' claims — another MQ-9 destroyed, mines hitting two tankers, three tankers halted on a route Tehran does not recognise — are a third consecutive day of mine claims no monitor has confirmed, logged as a pattern and unscored. UKMTO did confirm a tug struck by two projectiles off the UAE on Monday, October now the worst month for strait attacks since March. The coalition intercepted a ballistic missile and then a drone and missile aimed at Riyadh. Britain deployed RAF Typhoons for defensive counter-air operations over Saudi Arabia and said it would not strike Yemen — an executed force-posture act by a new actor, scored at the posture weight as the existing class and flagged as the first direct European military participation in the Saudi theatre; the class question is referred, and a new-class finding would be a two-point revision under the delegation. The Shabwa toll rose to 73. France secured 200,000 tonnes a month of diesel from the UAE and Bahrain overland via Oman — supply mitigation, transmission only. Qatar and Pakistan reportedly proposed interest on six billion dollars of frozen funds in exchange for an IAEA visit, with reported American approval and a positive Iranian response; the same day Pezeshkian said there would be no return to talks until the pressure campaign stops and Rezaei that not a gram of enriched material would leave Iran. A proposal with contradicting principals is process; it is logged prospectively as a resolution trigger — an executed visit or release moves the cell. Fifty-six acts. 10/7/77/6 stands. RECONCILIATION. Monday's yields are final within a basis point; Monday's oil is final at 103.83. The Bank of Canada posted Monday's benchmarks: the Government of Canada two-year rose twelve basis points to 3.33 on Canadian CPI day, the ten-year nine to 3.93, narrowing the two-year discount to the US to 144 basis points from 153 — the Canadian front end repricing while the American one did not. Consumer sentiment and the Chair's remarks are owed a third edition. TENURE NINE, THREE OF FOUR. Next: the December-based reference on Wednesday — the step-down is arithmetic, not a signal — the exchange's confirmation of tonight's settle, Kpler's next count, and whether anyone other than the Guards confirms a mine.

editions.summary: REVISION TWENTY-FIVE, ON AN OILFIELD. On Wednesday Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi drone aimed at Aramco's Shaybah field in the Empty Quarter and two people were killed in the interception, according to the energy ministry via Reuters. Monday's record flagged the Houthi claim on Shaybah prospectively: every Aramco act in the series to date had been downstream or corporate — Ras Tanura, Jubail, the Dhahran administrative building, the Riyadh headquarters — and a confirmed attack on upstream production would be a new target class. It is confirmed, with fatalities. The ledger scores it at the intercepted weight, two points, not the four a strike on the field itself would carry: escalation 77 to 79, stalemate 7 to 6, resolution 6 to 5, base held at 10 under the October 15 anchor record. The same day a Houthi attack on King Fahd International in Dammam killed one and injured eight — the airport class of revision #24, a repeat — the coalition destroyed four drones over the Eastern Province, and the State Department ordered non-emergency personnel out of Saudi Arabia, 'in Saudi Arabia only'. The ordered departure is an executed American consular act of a kind the series has not scored before; it is recorded under this revision as corroboration, not counted twice. Fifty-eight escalation acts. Ratification is requested. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure ten. THE ROLL. The first December-based reference prints 98.73: December settled 97.15, down 67 cents, and January is derived at 95.46 from a live quote's stated change, pending the exchange's final — the settlements feed was unreachable tonight after the fetch layer's rules changed with the session restart. The reference is $3.06 below Tuesday's November expiry settle, and the record states plainly that the step is arithmetic: the expiring contract carried a squeeze the deferred curve did not, and the day-over-day change in the oil field is not a market move. The channel is armed by $3.73. Brent settled 108.82 after topping 110 intraday and traded 110.11 early Thursday on the Saudi evacuation order. EIA crude stocks fell 3.1 million barrels against 0.8 expected. MARKETS. Technology and industrials led on SpaceX's $14.6 billion quarter and Super Micro's raised guide: Nasdaq up 1.05 percent to 26,702.76, S&P up 0.59 to 7,759.34, Dow up 0.69 to 52,864.83, Russell up a quarter; health care, staples and utilities lagged a day after leading; Netflix fell on guidance. The curve was flat to higher — two-year 4.81, ten-year 5.13, thirty-year 5.42 unchanged — with prediction markets at 88 percent for a hold next week and 11 for a hike. Mortgage applications fell 5.3 percent, purchases 7.3, with the thirty-year rate at 7.41. The VIX fell to 16.68, taking the Risk leg back off the line it touched Tuesday. The dollar weakened against all seven pairs for a third day; the loonie's fifth close below 1.42; the yen flat. Gold rose a third of a percent. THE STRAIT AND THE WORDS. Hormuz stays at 57.5 percent on Kpler's October 19 count, the latest dated measure; the Guards' claims of tankers set ablaze by mines are now contradicted by CENTCOM, which calls them false, while the IMO's secretary-general says it 'cannot guarantee' a transiting vessel will not be hit. Araghchi wrote in the FT that Iran 'seeks a just and honourable deal' and is 'fully prepared' to defend itself, and separately that there is 'little reason to expect progress'; Pezeshkian said Iran has submitted its plan and the US must meet its conditions; Tehran says Washington added clauses to the seven-day reopening plan; a Guards general threatened the seven undersea cables in the strait. Trump said the United States has 'decimated Iran', 'could leave now' but wants it to last, and is reported to be weighing direct strikes on the Houthis. Putin hosted Witkoff and offered to help. Words and deliberations; zero. RECONCILIATION AND HOUSEKEEPING. Tuesday's yields are final within two basis points; Tuesday's November expiry settle is confirmed at 101.79; the Bank of Canada posted Tuesday's benchmarks, the two-year at 3.32. Two long-owed items close: the consumer-sentiment gap was a calendar error — the preliminary October print was October 9, sentiment 46.3 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.7 and five-year at 3.5, the final due Friday — and no sourced Chair remarks exist for October 16, the blackout having begun the next day. TENURE TEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: the exchange's January final behind tonight's derived number; Tesla and Meta after the bell; Thursday's claims and existing home sales; whether Shaybah is attacked again; and whether a prospective resolution trigger that was contradicted within hours survives its first week.

editions.summary: THE TEN-YEAR BROKE BELOW FIVE; THE THIRTY-YEAR HELD. On a day the Nasdaq fell 2.6 percent on Meta's capital-spending guide and a six-percent semiconductor rout, the Treasury curve shifted down in parallel: the two-year fell sixteen basis points to 4.65, the ten-year seventeen to 4.96 — its largest one-day decline since March 2023, three weeks after it printed 5.36 — and the thirty-year thirteen to 5.29. The long-end channel is still armed, by twenty-nine basis points, the narrowest margin of the tenure; prediction markets price a 90 percent hold next week; initial claims were 194,000. The S&P fell 1.21 percent to 7,665.57 while the Dow and the Russell were flat — staples up three percent, utilities, health care, REITs and financials up one; the market sold the AI complex and bought everything rate-sensitive. The VIX closed 19.03 after 20.30 intraday, and the Risk leg moved back to TRANSITIONAL for the second time in a week. The yen rose 0.85 percent on the haven bid; the dollar was mixed; gold fell 2.6 percent and silver 4.7. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure eleven. OIL AND THE GUARDS' CLAIM. December WTI settled 99.47, up 2.4 percent, a five-month high; Brent settled 113.17, up four percent and its highest since May 4, after the Revolutionary Guards said seven oil tankers were struck in the strait in a single day — four set afire while transferring oil ship-to-ship, three disabled by mines — which would be the largest single-day toll of the war if true. No vessel is named and no monitor has confirmed it. A CENTCOM spokesperson told Al Jazeera the mine claims are incorrect, that the lanes are cleared, that Iran is using missiles and drones, and that 'the strait remains open, with 95 percent of vessels getting through'. The president wrote that Iran is 'making up fake hits, mines, and everything else' to drive oil up before the midterms and that more oil is moving through Hormuz than before the conflict. The ledger scores none of it: the Guards' claims are the fourth consecutive day without confirmation, the CENTCOM figure is a transit-success ratio rather than a flow measure and is recorded as a side field, and Hormuz stays at 57.5 percent on Kpler's October 19 count, three days old, until Monday's. The oil reference reads 101.00 on January carried at Wednesday's derived spread — two layers of provisionality, both flagged, with the exchange's finals for Wednesday and Thursday still unreachable; the channel is armed by six dollars at any plausible spread. The WTI–Brent spread widened to $13.70. HELD, BY RULE. The coalition intercepted and destroyed four drones over the Riyadh and Medina regions; the Houthis claimed forty-eight hours of attacks on the defence ministry, Abha, Yanbu and Dammam; the Dammam airport toll from Wednesday rose to two. Aramco ordered staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters, per Reuters and AFP sources — an executed corporate act, the second evacuation-class act in two days after the State Department's order, recorded as corroboration of yesterday's revision and scored zero. The Guards said that if the escorts continue 'the conflict will extend to [US] bases in the region'; the New York Times reported US and Israeli planning for a 'short but intensive' operation after the midterms, and Al Jazeera's correspondent in Tehran says the city expects an attack before November 3; the Guards' spokesman spoke of an 'offensive doctrine'; Netanyahu of regime change. Threats, reports and declarations. Fifty-nine acts. 10/6/79/5 stands. RECONCILIATION AND SOURCING. The Bank of Canada's ten-year for Wednesday is applied at 3.90, unchanged; the rest of the Canadian curve, Wednesday's H.15, both days' exchange finals and the VIX series remain owed under the fetch-layer rules. Existing home sales were not on the wire. The December reference's day-over-day change is now like-for-like. TENURE ELEVEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: whether the thirty-year follows the ten-year through five — the long-end channel is twenty-nine basis points from disarming on a day the Fed is expected to hold; Monday's strait count against a week of unverified claims; the Fed Tuesday-Wednesday; and whether anyone names a tanker.

editions.strategist_view: The ten-year went through five and the thirty-year stopped twenty-nine basis points short of it — on the day Brent settled at a five-month high on a claim nobody can verify. That is the label at its most stretched: the growth half priced in the curve and the AI complex, the cost-push half priced in Brent on words. The long-end channel is now the one most likely to lapse, and it would lapse from a rally, not a reversal. Two evacuation orders in two days moved nothing by rule. Tenure eleven.
editions.macro_view_client: The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 5% — its biggest one-day drop since 2023 — as technology stocks sold off on AI spending worries; the 30-year held at 5.29%, so our long-yield condition is still met, narrowly. Oil rose to a five-month high and Brent to its highest since May after Iran's Guards claimed seven tankers were struck in the strait, a claim the US military disputes. COST-PUSH / HAWKISH PIVOT held an eleventh day; scenarios held at 79% escalation.

editions.summary: OIL AT THE HIGHS OF THE SERIES. December WTI settled 103.27, up 3.8 percent, the highest front-month settle since April and 4.3 percent on the week; Brent 116.72, up 3.1 and 6.2 on the week. The catalysts were acts, not claims: a fire at Aramco's Yanbu facility after a Houthi strike — the first confirmed damage at an Aramco site since the Dhahran headquarters on October 13 — and a UKMTO-confirmed projectile strike on a tanker seven miles off Limah, Oman, on Thursday, which continued its voyage. UKMTO counts 57 of 79 projectile strikes since July on the southern route. The fair-value reference reads 104.75, with January carried for a third session on Wednesday's derived spread because the exchange's finals remain unreachable — flagged, band 104.14 to 105.46 — armed by $9.75 and $5.25 from the $110 line that turns the Supply reading ACUTE, the nearest it has been. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure twelve. THE FED REPRICED. The ten-year came back to 5.00, up four basis points; the thirty-year to 5.32, the long-end channel at 32 basis points; and the market now implies a 71 percent December hike after an October hold — the first sourced probability since September, replacing the figure the record had carried for seven weeks. Flash PMIs were strong: composite 57.6, manufacturing 56.0 against 55.5. Consumer sentiment's final October reading rose to 48.0, still the second-lowest on record, with one-year inflation expectations at 4.7 percent and five-year at 3.5, both confirmed from the preliminary. Equities fell a third day: the Dow 1.24 percent to 52,228.99, the S&P 0.52 to 7,625.77, the Nasdaq 0.21 as the AI complex bounced late; energy up 2.3 percent, eight of eleven sectors down; Fear & Greed at 20, extreme fear. The VIX closed 19.45; Risk stays TRANSITIONAL. Gold fell through $4,000 intraday to close 4000.88; the dollar was mixed. HELD, BY RULE. Three repeat-class acts: the Yanbu fire, the Limah strike, and Washington's designation of the Houthis as a terrorist organisation with a financial cut-off, the sanctions class. Sixty-two acts. Aramco's Dhahran evacuation is confirmed by Reuters and remains corroboration. The Guards claim four US-linked tankers struck on Thursday — a fifth consecutive day of claims no monitor has confirmed. The president said the United States 'could end the war very quickly', 'may do another little epic fury' if Iran will not deal, and 'could take all of the oil'; Netanyahu said the two countries must overthrow the regime and that Trump is 'ready to finish the job'; Waltz told the FT the war could last another year; Tehran said it would strike oil, cables, data centres and AI facilities in up to seven Gulf countries if attacked and that it has 'zero red lines', and Reuters reports detailed plans for the undersea cables. Words. A Russian diesel tanker sailing for the United States under the Trump-Putin arrangement is supply mitigation, transmission only. 10/6/79/5 stands. THE STRAIT, TWO NUMBERS APART. Treasury Secretary Bessent said Gulf crude exports have recovered above pre-conflict levels, showing a chart near 17 to 18 million barrels a day, and the president said 'Hormuz is totally ours'; Kpler's last weekly count, the engine's latest dated measure, put flows through the strait at 8.5 million. The engine stays at 57.5 percent because Treasury's chart is unattributed and outside the accepted source set; the divergence is the widest of the series and Monday's Kpler print is the test. If Kpler confirms Treasury, the chokepoint measure falls to the teens and the record will have carried a stale number for a week; if it confirms itself, the oil market has been right and the Treasury Secretary wrong. The record says which it is on Monday. RECONCILIATION. VIXCLS confirmed four days to the cent through a search-surfaced link. The exchange's oil finals for three sessions, the Fed's H.15 for three, and the Canadian curve remain owed under the fetch-layer rules; the operator's paste of those URLs clears them in one pass. TENURE TWELVE, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: the Fed on Wednesday with a hold priced and a December hike at 71; Monday's strait count; whether the thirty-year holds five into the decision; and whether the reference — $5 from ACUTE on a carried spread — gets its exchange finals back.

editions.summary: OIL EASED ON TALKS IN TEHRAN. December WTI settled 101.76, down 1.5 percent; Brent 115.81, down 0.8. The Saudi defence minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's army chief and the head of Turkish intelligence met Iran's president and its security council in Tehran — the Makkah-pact delegation, a day after Qatari mediators arrived — the first contact at that level since the war began. It is an executed meeting without an outcome: Tehran said it 'will not hesitate to exercise its inherent right to self-defense' and that Washington still demands 'complete surrender'; CNN reports US forces could strike within 96 hours of an order that most officials expect after the midterms. The fair-value reference reads 103.58, with January constructed from Friday's re-derived spread because the exchange's finals remain unreachable — provisional, band 103.32 to 103.87 — armed by $8.58 and $6.42 from the $110 line that turns Supply ACUTE. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure thirteen. THE CURVE BEAR-FLATTENED INTO THE FED. The two-year rose six basis points to 4.75 after a $69 billion auction tailed; the ten-year slipped to 4.99 and the thirty-year to 5.30, the long-end channel at 30 basis points. A hold is priced for Wednesday with roughly a one-in-ten chance of a hike; the December probability is carried at Friday's 71 for want of a Monday print. Equities rose on the AI complex — the S&P 0.70 percent to 7,676.80, re-based tonight to two agreeing sources after a week of chain divergence; the Nasdaq 0.82; semiconductors 3 — with more decliners than advancers on the day. Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq listing; Meta announced roughly $95 billion of equity for AI infrastructure; Musk said the debt markets have closed to data-centre operators without their own revenue. The VIX closed 18.30; Risk stays TRANSITIONAL at its nearest to RISK_ON of the tenure. The dollar was firm against six of seven pairs and the yen closed at 157.50, its weakest of the series. The S&P sits 5.2 percent above a 200-day average the record now computes each build. HELD, BY RULE. Three repeat-class acts: the weekend barrage on Saudi Arabia — two missiles intercepted near Mecca and Medina on Saturday; a ballistic missile and a drone over Riyadh, a cruise missile at Khamis Mushait and ten ballistic missiles in the south on Sunday, debris injuring two — Houthi missiles at Aden and Lahj with coalition strikes destroying five storage tunnels and four launchers on Monday; and Egypt's parliament approving military support to the kingdom. Sixty-five acts. The Tehran meeting is entered in the resolution column as a contact — sixty-five, seven, three — and does not move the weights: a revision on a meeting alone would be scoring a declaration; the class is for the operator. Riyadh's King Khalid airport reopened two terminals, closed since the October 10 attack that killed thirteen — restoration, corroborating. The Houthi warning that it remains 'a military target', Netanyahu's pre-election warning, Katz's 'no intention', the strike-readiness report and the Houthi claims on three airports and a pipeline are words. 10/6/79/5 stands. THE STRAIT, RE-BASED. Kpler's October-to-date average is 11.7 million barrels a day, up from 9.8 in September and close to February's 14.5; on the record's 20-million basis that is 41.5 percent disrupted, down from 57.5, and under the latest-observation rule it is the field. Friday's divergence resolves: Treasury's 17 to 18 million is total Gulf exports — the strait's 11.7 plus roughly 7 through the East-West pipeline, which Aramco's Nasser says has gone from 2 to 7 — a definition difference, not a contradiction. Three rulings are open: whether an October average is the right window against the weekly count the rule has used; whether the denominator is 20 or Kpler's own 14.5, which would read 19.3; and whether PortWatch's four transits on October 18 — a 95 percent reading, older-dated, from an AIS count that misses the dark transits INTERTANKO puts above thirty a day — remains admissible. None of the three moves the Supply leg, which is oil-driven. RECONCILIATION. H.15 confirmed Friday's curve to the basis point, the thirty-year a point higher at 5.33. The Bank of Canada's Friday benchmarks are applied — 3.33, 3.56, 3.83, 4.12 — and the TSX is sourced at 35,944.16 after sixteen editions carried. Friday's January leg was re-derived from a live quote, lifting Friday's reference to 105.31. The exchange's oil finals for four sessions, VIXCLS for three, the ICE dollar row and the Canadian bill remain owed. TENURE THIRTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: Israel votes Tuesday; the Fed Wednesday with the ECB and Bank of Japan the same week; whether the Tehran contact produces an act; GDP Thursday and PCE Friday; and whether the thirty-year holds five through the decision.

editions.summary: OIL BELOW $100 ON THE FRONT AS A FIRE BURNED AT RAS TANURA. December WTI settled 99.90, down 1.8 percent; Brent 113.88, down 1.7 — a second session lower on the Tehran track, where Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey and Iran 'agreed to keep talking' and Tehran described itself as 'flexible' on a proposal to reopen the strait in exchange for the US blockade lifting within seven days. The market sold the diplomacy through the act: Saudi Arabia intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles toward the Eastern Province early Tuesday and Aramco contained a fire near its Ras Tanura facilities — the kingdom's largest export terminal and refinery complex — the second confirmed Aramco-site fire in five days after Yanbu. The fire rests on one source with knowledge; the intercepts are official; the Houthi claim of 'massive fires' at the refinery is a claim. The fair-value reference reads 101.65, with January constructed from Friday's re-derived spread for a second session — provisional, band 101.40 to 102.15 — armed by $6.65 and $8.35 from the $110 line that turns Supply ACUTE. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure fourteen. THE RISK LEG FLIPPED. The VIX closed 17.52, down 4.7 percent, and the Risk dimension moved from TRANSITIONAL to RISK_ON — the flip Monday's record flagged at a boundary of 0.04 — with the composite unaffected. The S&P rose 0.60 percent to 7,722.60, within 1.2 percent of its high and 5.8 percent above a 200-day the record computes each build; the Nasdaq 1.18, semiconductors 3.6 a second day, the Russell 1.16; equal-weight 0.11. The Conference Board index printed 91.7 against 81.0 expected, ten points above consensus three days after the Michigan survey's second-lowest reading on record; durable goods rose 1.8 percent; new home sales 676,000. The curve held into the Fed — 4.75, 5.00, 5.31, the long-end channel 31 basis points — with a hold priced near 90 percent and a December hike at 82, the engine's policy input updated from Friday's 71. The dollar rose a third session to a two-week high; the yen closed 157.93, its weakest of the series; gold 4,062. HELD, BY RULE. One repeat-class act: Ras Tanura with its intercepts, the Saudi-infrastructure class, sixty-six on the ledger, the fire flagged single-source. The resolution column stays at three: the four parties' agreement to keep talking and Putin's meeting with Pezeshkian are contacts; Iran's seven-day proposal is a proposal; Khamenei's conditions, the president's 'getting to be decision time' and the Houthis' 'declaration of war' on Egypt are words. Israel voted: the exit polls give Netanyahu's bloc about fifty seats and the opposition fifty-two to fifty-three with the Arab parties at seventeen — no majority either way, official results November 4, a mandate by November 11 — and Netanyahu's 'topple the regime' against Eisenkot's 'not achievable' is the Iran question on the ballot; the record scores an election zero until a government forms. 10/6/79/5 stands. THE RECONCILIATION LAYER STALLED. Every allowed link served a stale vintage tonight: the Fed's H.15 page returned Monday's release, the Bank of Canada's series the Friday row, the exchange's JSON refused. Monday's yields, the Canadian curve for two days, VIXCLS for four and the oil finals for five sessions are owed, and Monday's VIX close is itself disputed — 18.30 recorded, 18.39 in tonight's source — for the official series to settle. The TSX is an intraday print, flagged rather than carried. The strait holds at 41.5 on Kpler's October average, two days old, with two unattributed higher readings — 'about 65 percent of pre-conflict' and 'around prewar levels' — logged beside it and outside the set. TENURE FOURTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: the Fed at two on Wednesday with the hold priced and the statement's hike language the variable; whether the Tehran track produces an act or the president's 'decision time' does; GDP Thursday, PCE Friday; the ECB and Bank of Japan; and the operator's paste of the H.15, Valet and CME links.

editions.summary: THE FED HELD WITH TWO HAWKISH DISSENTS AND THE BANK OF CANADA HIKED. The FOMC kept the funds range at 3.75 to 4.00 on a 10–2 vote, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting for a quarter-point increase — Cook's the surprise. The statement upgraded growth from 'solid' to 'strong', kept 'inflation remains elevated', and added that 'the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance'. Warsh called the meeting 'a strong family fight', said the 'monetary medicine was starting to work', declined to prejudge December and repeated that he does not believe in forward guidance absent a crisis. Money markets price December near 85 percent, from 82. North of the border the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 2.50 — the first increase since July 2023 — with inflation around 3 percent since April and seen at 3½ by year-end, growth at 1 percent this year, and 'there could be a need to increase the policy rate further'. The Fed–BoC spread narrows to 150 basis points; the loonie closed below 1.40 for the first time in the episode. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure fifteen. THE CURVE BEAR-STEEPENED AND OIL REBOUNDED. The two-year fell a basis point to 4.72 and the thirty-year rose five to 5.36 — the long-end channel at 36 basis points — a curve that read the dissents as a Fed that will hike into a term premium. December WTI settled 102.78, up 2.9 percent, with an intraday high at 103.55, after the Wall Street Journal reported Washington had told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterms (NewsNation disputes that the Gulf states were told), Iran's Fars agency circulated satellite imagery it says shows significant damage to the 550,000-barrel main refining unit at Ras Tanura (Saudi Arabia has not confirmed; if it does, Tuesday's act upgrades from a contained fire to damage at the kingdom's largest refinery), and the coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Taif. UBS lifted its forecasts to Brent near $110 through year-end on record freight and depleted reserve releases. The fair-value reference reads 104.45, with January constructed from Friday's spread for a third session — provisional, band 104.22 to 104.94 — armed by $9.45 and $5.55 from the $110 line that turns Supply ACUTE. Brent's quoted contract rolled to January at 111.64, not a chained move. HELD, BY RULE. Two repeat-class acts: the Taif intercept and two Houthi ballistic-missile attacks on Aden airport. Sixty-eight. The Fed's hold and the Bank of Canada's hike are policy inputs — they move the Policy dimension's data, not the ledger. The Fars imagery and the Houthi claim on Abha airport are claims. Reuters says Qatari mediators presented Tehran a new draft on Sunday with a response due by week-end; other reports and Iranian officials deny a draft was presented; the Journal reports the vice president reached out to an Iranian hardliner; Axios reports mediators warning Tehran that acceptance may be its only way to avert major attacks; Araghchi says Iran 'continues to give diplomacy a chance' and that an Israeli-instigated escalation 'could have a devastating impact on international markets'. Reports and words. Israel's count continues with early returns leaning to Netanyahu's bloc against exit polls that had it short of sixty-one — an electoral event the record scores zero until a government forms. 10/6/79/5 stands. EQUITIES HELD A TWENTY-FIVE-POINT RANGE THROUGH THE FED. The S&P closed 7,743.98, up 0.28 percent; the Nasdaq 0.27; semiconductors 1.75 on SK Hynix's beat; equal-weight flat; seven of eleven sectors up with utilities and real estate down on the long end. After the close Alphabet fell 7 percent and Microsoft rose 4 on earnings; Oracle rose 10 on a capital-raising cap. The VIX closed near 17.20 and the Risk leg holds RISK_ON; gold 4,070; the dollar fell after the presser to 102.13 with the loonie's best day of the month. The S&P sits 6.1 percent above its 200-day. RECONCILIATION. Nothing cleared a second night: the Fed's page still serves Monday's release, the Bank of Canada's series Friday's row, the exchange refuses; the TSX close did not surface and the December Brent settle is replaced in the wires by January. Monday's yields and now Tuesday's and Wednesday's, the Canadian curve for three days, VIXCLS for five, the oil finals for six sessions and the Brent roll are owed. The strait holds at 41.5 on Kpler's October average, three days old, with UBS's 'improving, not yet fully normalised' logged beside it. TENURE FIFTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: GDP and PCE Thursday; the ECB; whether Tehran answers the draft it says it has not received; whether Riyadh confirms Ras Tanura; Israel's count; and the operator's paste of the H.15, Valet and CME links, now three legs and nine sessions deep.

editions.summary: GDP 3.4 ON A PCE 3.6. The third-quarter advance estimate printed 3.4 percent annualised against 3.1 expected and the second quarter's 2.2, with consumer spending up 3.8 percent and the quarter's PCE price index at 2.1 against 2.6 — a hot real print with a cool deflator. September's monthly PCE rose 0.5 percent, core 0.3, both as expected; the year-on-year rates ran 3.6 and 3.1, both a tenth higher than August. Claims held 194,000. The front end bought the deflator: the two-year fell eight basis points to 4.65, the ten-year five to 4.99, the thirty-year three to 5.33, the long-end channel at 33 basis points; December stays priced near 85. The ECB held all three rates and signalled nothing, calling energy an upside risk to inflation and a downside risk to growth. The engine's growth input moves from 1.6 to 3.4 and the Growth dimension flips from SLOWING to BIFURCATED at a boundary of exactly zero — the tag is on the line and is flagged; the composite is unchanged. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure sixteen. ALPHABET TOOK THE NASDAQ DOWN; THE RUSSELL MADE A THREE-WEEK HIGH. Alphabet fell 12 percent — search growth of 12 percent against the Street's 15, free cash flow negative $9.1 billion — and the Nasdaq lost 1.38 percent to 26,184.72; ServiceNow fell 15, Fortinet 20; Microsoft beat on Azure and free cash flow and launched a bond offering; after the close Amazon fell 6.7 percent and Intel 17.6. And yet NYSE breadth ran nearly two-to-one positive, eight of eleven sectors rose, REITs 2 percent, and the Russell gained 1.01 percent to 2,859.19. The S&P closed 7,720.22, down 0.31; the VIX 16.42 and the Risk leg holds RISK_ON. The AI-capex trade is now a two-way market and the index is wider than its leaders. Oil drifted: December WTI 102.00, down 0.8 percent, and Brent's January contract 110.63, despite Iran's army claiming four tankers afire on mines on the 'unauthorised southern route' and UKMTO confirming one vessel — a dhow — burning and sinking nine miles off Khasab. The reference reads 103.60 with January constructed for a fourth session — provisional, band 103.38 to 104.06 — armed by $8.60 and $6.40 from the $110 line. Gold fell 1.2 percent; the euro touched a seventeen-month low near 1.11 after the ECB; the loonie held below 1.40 a second day. HELD, BY RULE. Two repeat-class acts: the Khasab vessel, the shipping class; and the coalition's intercepts — one ballistic missile at the Eastern Province before dawn, two at Riyadh after dark. Seventy. The Vance letter to Supreme National Security Council chief Rezaei — received in Tehran, unanswered, the first direct US–Iran written contact of the series — is entered in the resolution column as a contact and does not move the weights; the president says it concerned medical supplies, Axios says the nuclear programme. A senior Iranian official called Qatar's ideas 'unacceptable and not an offer'; Araghchi is 'discussing a seven-day plan' whose terms are unfrozen assets, oil-sanctions relief and the end of the blockade; Ghalibaf says progress depends on seven conditions. Two diplomats say allies were told to prepare for post-midterm strikes; Gulf News reports a week-long campaign; the Joint Staff removed its strategy chief and withdrew the statement. Words and reports. Fars' Ras Tanura imagery is a second day unconfirmed. Israel's count at over 90 percent: Netanyahu 53, the opposition 48, the Arab parties 19 — no majority; zero until a government forms. 10/6/79/5 stands. TWO STALE INPUTS, FOUND AND FIXED. Today's release exposed that the engine's GDP field had sat at 1.6 since May 28 — the second quarter's 2.2 was never applied — and its headline PCE at 4.1 since June 25: four months, the same failure class as the 200-day, logged as integrity finding #7 and now maintained from the release calendar. Neither moved a tag before today; today the GDP input does, and the record says so. VIXCLS cleared five sessions through a search-surfaced link — Monday corrected to 18.39, Wednesday to 16.91, no tag effect — and Wednesday's disputed WTI settle is confirmed at 102.78 by today's chain. Official yields for four sessions, the Canadian curve for four, the exchange's oil finals for seven and the TSX close for three remain owed. TENURE SIXTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5. Next: payrolls next Friday and the midterms Tuesday as the implied strike deadline; Tehran's answer to a plan it calls unacceptable; Riyadh on Ras Tanura; Israel's final count; and whether the Growth tag holds on a boundary of zero.

editions.summary: DAY 200 — A HALLOWEEN SELL-OFF IN TECH. Intel fell 29 percent, its steepest day on record, on a fourth-quarter guide of $15 to 16 billion against $17.3 and PC revenue down a fifth; Amazon fell 2 after $75.9 billion of quarterly capital spending, a reiterated $220 billion for the year and trailing free cash flow of negative $42 billion; Meta's free cash flow went negative for the first time since 2012; semiconductors lost 7.2 percent on the day and 15.3 on the month. The Nasdaq fell 2.86 percent to 25,437.00 — its worst month since March 2025 and roughly two trillion dollars off the Nasdaq-100 in October — the S&P 1.82 to 7,580.07, a third straight weekly decline, the longest run since March; the Dow 1.09, the Russell 1.66. The VIX spiked to 23.93 in the afternoon, above the October 16 high, and closed 19.42: the Risk leg flips back from RISK_ON to TRANSITIONAL, its second flip in a week, with the composite unchanged. And yet nine of eleven sectors rose on the month — energy 13 percent, health, utilities and staples more than 10 — as Exxon and Chevron printed record refining profits and 52-week highs. The index is wider than its leaders; the leaders are what fell. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure seventeen. OIL AT A SIX-WEEK HIGH, $4.35 FROM ACUTE. December WTI settled 104.12, up 2.1 percent, the highest close since September 15 and 12 percent on the month; December Brent expired at 117.64, the highest since April and 15 percent on the month, a fourth monthly gain. UKMTO corrected Thursday night's incident: a tanker was hit by explosive devices attached to its hull by a small boat — a limpet attack, the first of its kind in the series. The Houthis claimed strikes on Ras Tanura, the Rabigh refinery and the Abqaiq processing facility; the coalition confirmed intercepting a cruise missile toward the western region; the Guards claimed another tanker mined on an 'unauthorised route'. The fair-value reference reads 105.65, with January constructed from the October 23 spread for a fifth session — provisional, band 105.43 to 106.09 — armed by $10.65 and the nearest to the $110 line of the entire series: a December settle near $108.60 turns Supply ACUTE. Gold fell 3.3 percent to 3,883, a 52-week low and 30 percent below January's record; silver 5.9. THE CURVE BULL-STEEPENED A SECOND DAY. The two-year fell 7.5 basis points to 4.58, the ten-year 6 to 4.93, the thirty-year 2 to 5.31, the long-end channel at 31 basis points; on the month the two-year is 31 lower and the ten-year 36. This is a market pricing a Fed that holds its hikes into a slowdown it can see in semiconductors — two days after that Fed held with two dissents for a rise. December is carried at 85 for want of a Friday print; the front end argues lower and the record says so. The employment cost index rose 0.8 percent as expected; Chicago PMI 55.3 against 56.0. The dollar was soft against six of seven; the loonie closed below 1.40 a third day; the yen gained for the first time in a week. HELD, BY RULE. Two repeat-class acts: the limpet attack, the shipping class with a new sub-type; and the cruise-missile intercept. Seventy-two. The Houthi claims on Ras Tanura, Rabigh and Abqaiq are claims — Abqaiq would be a new target class, the facility whose 2019 strike took 5.7 million barrels a day offline, and the record watches for a Saudi damage statement; Fars' Ras Tanura imagery is a third day unconfirmed. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran; an Iranian official 'welcomes any efforts aimed at negotiations'; Tasnim says the Vance letter is unanswered and anything outside Iran's framework 'unacceptable'; the president says the war 'will end soon' and that there will be no strikes before the polls. Contacts and words. Israel's final count is pending. 10/6/79/5 stands. RECONCILIATION. The archive base changed tonight: the operator's n112_f7_cr1 — the finding-#7 back-fill plus the credit layer on all 112 editions — was adopted and hash-verified before the build, and Edition 113's credit fields are owed to the credit-layer session. Thursday's VIX is corrected to 17.20 from an intraday print; Thursday's WTI settle is confirmed by today's chain. The TSX is a headline estimate, a fourth session without a close. Official yields for five sessions, the Canadian curve for five, the exchange's oil finals for eight and the Brent January settles since the roll remain owed. The strait holds at 41.5 on Kpler's October average, five days old; no weekly print surfaced this week. TENURE SEVENTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5, DAY 200. Next: the midterms Tuesday as the implied strike deadline; OPEC+ Sunday; payrolls Friday; ISM Monday; whether Riyadh confirms Abqaiq; whether the two-year's 31-basis-point October is the market telling the Fed something; and the reference $4.35 from the line.

editions.strategist_view: Two hundred days. The leaders fell and the market did not: semiconductors lost seven percent, Intel a third, and nine of eleven sectors finished October higher. The Risk leg flipped back on a spike to twenty-four that closed under twenty — positioning, not a regime. The number that matters is the reference, four dollars and thirty-five cents from the line that turns Supply acute, on the day of the strait's first limpet attack and a claim on Abqaiq. Tenure seventeen.

editions.summary: OIL FELL 7.4 PERCENT ON A MANDATE. December WTI settled 96.46, down 7.66, and Brent's January 104.77, down 7.63 percent — the largest one-day falls since July — after President Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Khamenei 'has also granted certain powers to the government' to resolve the war through dialogue, the first sovereign negotiating mandate of the conflict. Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei said talks proceed on Iran's seven-step proposal, under which the strait reopens within days of US compliance — Araghchi on Saturday said two; Iranian officials say energy transport will be eased and formal talks resume once the blockade lifts; the delegation remains in Doha and a draft is circulating. The president said Iran wants to 'make a deal', that one or two targets still need to be 'taken care of', and that strikes could resume after Tuesday's midterms; per Axios he told Netanyahu he is open to more time. OPEC+ held December targets on Sunday. The fair-value reference reads 97.53, with January constructed from Friday's recovered 1.91 spread — provisional, band 97.30 to 97.77 — and sits $2.53 above the $95 line that arms the oil channel: one more session like this one and the transmission count falls to two of four. Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot, tenure eighteen. THE INDEX FELL AND THE MARKET ROSE. The S&P closed 7,541.40, down 0.51 percent, the Nasdaq 1.07, as technology lost 2.95 percent and energy 3.96 — while the equal-weight index rose 0.76, mid-caps 0.80, small-caps 0.78, consumer discretionary 2.41 and financials 1.86, with 1,027 gainers against 473 decliners across the four indices. A second consecutive week in which the capitalisation-weighted index and the median stock disagree; the S&P sits 3.1 percent above a 200-day the record computes each build. The VIX rose 8.9 percent to 21.15 and the Risk leg holds TRANSITIONAL, now deep in its band. ISM manufacturing printed 55.5 against 54.5 — a tenth month of expansion, production at its highest since November 2021 — with prices paid easing to 75.2 from 77.9; construction spending fell 1.9 percent, the steepest since April 2020. The long end rallied: ten-year 4.89, thirty-year 5.27, the channel at 27 basis points; December's hike repriced from 85 to 72 percent on the oil move. Gold rose 1.6 percent off Friday's 52-week low; the franc was bid; the loonie held below 1.40 a fourth day. Apple reported $114.5 billion. HELD, BY RULE — AND THE RULE IS PUT TO THE OPERATOR. Three repeat-class acts from Saturday: a Qatari LNG tanker struck in the Arabian Gulf, confirmed by Doha and condemned by Kuwait and Riyadh — the first LNG carrier of the series; a UKMTO-confirmed projectile strike on a vessel in Hormuz; a coalition intercept of a Houthi ballistic missile. Seventy-five. The Khamenei mandate is entered in the resolution column as the fifth contact. The standing rule scores declarations at zero and moves weights only on executed acts — a text, a protocol, a ceasefire; by that rule a grant of authority to negotiate is a declaration, and 10/6/79/5 stands. The oil market scored it as an act, at seven percent. The record does not resolve that disagreement by itself: it asks the operator whether a sovereign mandate grant is an act. If it is, revision #26 opens — indicatively 10/6/74/10, moving five points from escalation to resolution on the symmetry of the October 21 revision; if it is not, the next act is a text and the weights wait for it. The Houthi threats against Aramco and Saudi aviation, the Hodeidah strike report, the unverified tanker-and-tug report and Khamenei's 'without geographical limits' are words and claims; Abqaiq is a fourth day without a Saudi damage statement. THE GAP-CLOSURE SWEEP. On the operator's instruction the owed list was worked before the build. H.15 is confirmed for five sessions through FRED's series pages — the two-year runs four to seven basis points below the wire provisionals it replaces, the ten- and thirty-year within a point — and VIXCLS for two. The Bank of Canada's ten-year is confirmed for Monday to Thursday, the two-year for Thursday, the five-year and long bond for Friday; the rest of the curve and the bill remain owed. The TSX close is sourced for Friday at 35,620.03 — a 629-point fall where the headline estimate had 200 — and the earlier week re-derived. Friday's January WTI settle was recovered at 102.21, a 1.91 spread against the 2.33 the constructs had assumed since October 23, so Friday's reference is 105.37 rather than 105.65 and the earlier constructs are flagged. Friday's Brent January settle was 113.42. The EIA's Cushing spot series is logged as the physical cross-check the oil ADR calls for. The credit layer's funding legs are instrumented for the first time — SOFR 3.94 against IORB 3.90, bills 4.00, commercial paper 4.05. Still owed: the exchange's own finals for eight sessions, Friday's thirty-year, half the Canadian curve, the TSX for Wednesday and today, the ICE dollar row, and Friday's high-yield and investment-grade prints. TENURE EIGHTEEN, THREE OF FOUR, 10/6/79/5, DAY 201. Next: the midterms Tuesday; the operator's ruling on the mandate; whether the reference holds $95; Tehran's seven-step text or its absence; Israel's government; payrolls Friday.

editions.summary: REVISION #26. Late Monday evening, after the close, the Revolutionary Guard fired a surface-to-air missile at an American aircraft over the Strait of Hormuz — Iranian media published imagery of a downed MQ-9 — and a US fighter destroyed the launcher on Qeshm Island. Three US officials described the strikes to CBS as limited and defensive; officials confirmed them to Reuters; the President, on Fox, said the US had hit an anti-aircraft facility 'very nicely' and was 'not looking to kill lots of people, but if we have to, we'll have to'. Israel said it was not involved. The Wall Street Journal, which broke the story, described it as the latest in a series of low-profile strikes kept quiet precisely so as not to signal a resumption of the campaign. A direct kinetic exchange between US and Iranian forces on Iranian territory is a class this record has not scored — its only prior US kinetic act is a dhow destroyed in the Gulf of Oman on October 6 — and a new class opens a revision under the standing rule, as Shaybah did on October 21. It is sized at the posture weight, two points, rather than the kinetic four: Washington bounded the act in the same breath ('not the start of expanded strikes'; Trump's 'no' when asked about strikes after the midterms), and the market scored it at a dollar intraday and nothing by the close. Escalation 79 to 81, stalemate 6 to 4. Resolution is held at 5 on purpose: the question whether Sunday's mandate grant is an act is still with the operator, and cutting the resolution cell the day after asking whether to raise it would prejudge the answer. The four-point case is recorded for the ratifier — a destroyed launcher is damage, not an interception. Repeat classes: a vessel attacked off Oman with one Indian sailor killed, per India's minister; coalition drone intercepts over Mecca and the south. Iran's claim that three tankers struck mines, the Guard's claim of two drones captured, and the Houthi casualty figures are claims. Ledger 78/7/5/0. OIL SHRUGGED AT THE STRIKE AND LEANED ON THE DRAFT. December WTI settled 96.09, down 0.4 percent and a four-week low; Brent's January 103.60, down 1.1 percent across a six-dollar range — up a dollar on the Qeshm report, down on the diplomacy. Qatar said it was 'bridging the gap' and that both sides were reviewing a draft, with feedback expected within 36 hours; Al Araby reported, from a single source, that Washington had approved the Qatar-presented memorandum; the President wrote 'Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible. It could happen!' A senior Iranian official told Reuters a deal was 'still out of reach' and that the US response had not been 'satisfactory'; AP reports Netanyahu pressing for another wave of strikes. None of it is a text, and none of it moves the weights. The fair-value reference reads 97.10 — January constructed a second time on Friday's recovered 1.91 spread, provisional — $2.10 above the $95 line that arms the oil channel: armed, at risk, one more session like Monday's from switching off. Bloomberg notes the nearest Dubai timespread has gone to contango and Gulf flows ex-Iran rose ten percent in October to above 15 million barrels a day; the Oman–Dubai premium that was thirty dollars in September is near zero. key_events: THE LABEL CHANGED ON THE BALLOT, NOT THE BATTLEFIELD: Democrats won both chambers of Congress and oil fell more than eight percent — December WTI 88.12, its lowest since August 31, Brent 94.62, below $100 for the first time since October 7 — as traders bet the result shortens the war; the fair-value reference reads 89.08, provisional, $0.92 below the $90 edge of the persistent band, so the Supply leg moves to EASING and the composite to Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot after nineteen sessions of Cost-Push; the oil channel disarms ($5.92 below $95) and transmission falls to two of four; the state does not depend on the constructed January leg — December itself settled below $90 — but the same strict edge flipped the label on October 6 and reverted it two sessions later, and the engine still has no band at $90

editions.summary: THE LABEL CHANGED ON THE BALLOT. Democrats won the House and the Senate on Tuesday, and on Wednesday oil fell more than eight percent: December WTI settled 88.12, down 7.97 and its lowest since August 31; Brent's January 94.62, down 8.98, below $100 for the first time since October 7 and its largest one-day fall since April. Traders read the result as a constraint on the war — BOK Financial's Kissler said Democratic control could tighten military spending and bring a deal sooner — while CIBC's Babin called the move 'a bit overdone' and Rapidan's McNally said 'Iran is hardened'. Crude inventories drew 865,000 barrels against an expected build. The fair-value reference reads 89.08 — January constructed a third time on Friday's recovered 1.91 spread, provisional, band 88.86 to 89.30 — which is $0.92 below the $90 edge of the persistent band. The Supply leg moves to EASING and the composite, after nineteen sessions, to DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT: inflation still running cost-push at 3.7 percent, a Fed still priced 77 percent to hike in December, and the oil that drove both now retreating. The oil channel disarms, $5.92 below $95, and transmission falls to two of four — the long end and CPI. TWO THINGS ABOUT THAT CHANGE. First, it does not rest on the construct: December itself settled at 88.12, so the state holds for any December–January spread below $3.76. Second, it rests on a round number with no band around it. The same $90 edge flipped this label on October 6 at 89.90 and flipped it back on October 8 at 91.78; the observation that the frozen engine has no hysteresis at $90 has been in the ratification queue since that week. The record applies the rule as written — a band is a change to the engine, not a judgment the daily build may make — and states that $0.92 on a provisional reference is the thinnest margin a label change can stand on. Robustness falls with tenure to its floor. THE WEIGHTS DID NOT MOVE. No act was confirmed. The Revolutionary Guard said four tankers had been destroyed by mines south of the strait on a 'prohibited passage' and two more stopped — the third such claim in four days, uncorroborated by UKMTO or CENTCOM, which has said the main routes are clear — and that it downed a US Reaper over the strait; Washington did not comment. Two drones struck a Kurdish opposition base in northern Iraq, launcher unstated. The Supreme Leader said anyone expecting a change in American policy is 'seriously mistaken' and that renewed attacks would widen the war; Ghalibaf wrote that Americans 'said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message'; Iran's security council called the US reply 'not convincing'. The President said 'part of it was Iran' and that he 'would have done it again'; the New York Times reports him weighing renewed strikes; the Vice President said 'the reason we lost is the war'. Qatar's 36-hour window on the draft runs into Thursday. 10/4/81/5. A disinflation label under a scenario set weighted 81 percent to escalation is not a contradiction: the label moves on transmission and the weights on acts, and the gap between them is the information — the market has priced a political constraint the act rule does not score. The mandate-class ruling and the ratification of revision #26 remain with the operator. THE BROADEST DAY OF THE AUTUMN. The Dow rose 3.03 percent, 1,569 points, its best session after a midterm in 44 years; the S&P 1.58 percent to 7,688.62; the Nasdaq 1.44; the Russell 1.58; the equal-weight index 1.86. 1,122 stocks advanced against 379. Discretionary rose 4.3 percent, financials 3.5, communications, staples and real estate 3.3 to 3.5, health care 3.1; energy fell 4.7. The VIX dropped 20 percent to 16.61 and the Risk leg moves to RISK_ON. Gold rose 3.5 percent to $4,058, silver 5.4. The curve rallied — two-year 4.58, ten-year 4.89, thirty-year 5.28 — and December's hike eased to 77 percent. The dollar softened against six of seven; the loonie went back below 1.40. ADP added 86,000; ISM services printed 54.5 with new orders down four points to 55.9; the September trade deficit narrowed to $105 billion. The TSX rose 2.3 percent to 36,341. THE BOOKS. Tuesday's official two- and ten-year and VIX confirmed to the basis point; Monday's thirty-year 5.28; Tuesday's high-yield spread 340. Still owed: the exchange's January finals, Tuesday's thirty-year, the Canadian curve, and the trackers' strait print, ten days old. TENURE ONE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/81/5, DAY 203. Next: Qatar's window; whether December holds below $90 — the label's second session; the two rulings; payrolls Friday.

editions.strategist_view: Nineteen sessions of Cost-Push ended on an election, not an event in the Gulf, and I would rather say that plainly than dress it up: the rule moved the label because December settled at 88, and the rule is right to — but it is the same $90 edge that flipped us on October 6 and back two days later, and the engine still has no band there. The weights stayed put because nobody confirmed anything at sea. The honest read is a market that has repriced the political constraint on the war while the war itself has not changed. Tenure one.
editions.macro_view_client: Oil fell more than 8% — WTI $88.12, Brent $94.62, the lowest since late August — after Democrats won both chambers of Congress and markets priced a shorter war; our physical reference is $89.08, provisional. Our regime reading changes to DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT after nineteen sessions of Cost-Push: inflation is still elevated and a December Fed hike is still priced at 77%, but the oil shock behind it is now retreating, and two of four transmission conditions remain. Stocks rallied broadly — the Dow +3%, advancers outnumbering decliners three to one. Scenarios unchanged at 81% escalation: no new act was confirmed.

editions.summary: THE LABEL WENT BACK. December WTI rebounded 2.7 percent to 90.52 and Brent's January 3.9 percent to 98.29 after Wednesday's eight-percent fall, which CIBC's Babin called a 'mass liquidation event'. The fair-value reference reads 91.42 — January constructed a fourth time on Friday's recovered 1.91 spread, provisional — $1.42 above the $90 edge of the persistent band. The Supply leg returns to PERSISTENT and the composite to COST-PUSH / HAWKISH PIVOT, one session after it left. December itself settled above $90, so the reversal does not depend on the construct. This is the second one-session round trip on that edge: October 6 to 8 was the first. The frozen engine has no band at $90, the record applies the rule as written, and it files ADR-HY-001 today — a proposed hysteresis layer for the thresholds that command the label, back-tested on the archive. The oil channel stays off, $3.58 below $95; transmission holds at two of four. THE WORST DAY SINCE APRIL 2025. The S&P fell 4.35 percent to 7,353.73; the Nasdaq 5.5 percent into correction, about $2 trillion of market value; the Nasdaq-100 6.4; the semiconductor index 11 to 12 percent, its second-worst day on record — Nvidia down 9, AMD and Micron 17, SanDisk 22. The driver, per Reuters and the Seeking Alpha and Motley Fool desks, was a repricing of AI data-centre build-outs against a Democratic Congress — permitting, power bills, funding — on positioning already crowded and valuations stretched; Citadel's model had CTA equity exposure at its lowest since March. The equal-weight index fell 2.9 percent, outperforming the cap-weighted index by 146 basis points: a liquidation concentrated where the capital was. The VIX rose 70 percent to 28.18, its highest close since March, and the Risk leg moves to RISK_OFF. The S&P sits 0.4 percent above its 200-day; Market Structure reads TECHNICAL_NEUTRAL. RATES RALLIED FROM THE FRONT. The two-year fell 11.5 basis points to 4.47, the ten-year five to 4.84, the thirty-year two to 5.26 — a sharp bull steepening — and December's hike repriced from 77 to 69 percent, Reuters noting the next move is not fully priced until March. The data argued the other way: jobless claims 189,000, matching a 57-year low; third-quarter productivity up 3.6 percent and unit labour costs down 0.7. Barkin and Hammack both described gradual hikes as the path. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25 basis points to 4.00 percent, its first hike since 2023, and Bailey said there is a case for another if the war does not end. Gold rose 1.4 percent to $4,114; the Aussie fell 0.9 percent; the loonie returned to 1.40; the TSX fell 2.0 percent. REVISION #27: 10/4/76/10. The operator ruled this evening that Sunday's grant of negotiating authority by the Supreme Leader to the government is an act, not a declaration; the resolution scenario takes the five points from escalation that the record indicated when it put the question on Monday. Revision #26 and the resolution hold were ratified in the same ruling. UKMTO confirmed a tanker hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar late Wednesday — a repeat shipping act; ledger 79/7/5/0. Iran's Revolutionary Guard and army claimed five tankers and a tugboat set ablaze by mines on 'unauthorized routes' — unverified, the fourth such claim in five days. The New York Times reports thousands of US air and naval forces positioned to resume combat on order; the President said he has no immediate plans to strike and that the US remains prepared to. Eurasia Group cut its deal odds from 20 to 10 percent. None of today's events moves the weights; the ruling does. THE FIRST EODHD EDITION. Index closes, the VIX, the ICE dollar index, the Treasury par curve, ETF bars and the news feed now come through the EODHD layer. On its first pass it closed the ICE dollar row that had been owed for weeks, the TSX closes for October 28 and November 2, and Tuesday's thirty-year. On the operator's directive the archive was corrected from official closes across 105 editions; no historical regime label changed. TENURE ONE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 204. editions.summary: PAYROLLS BLEW OUT. October added 165,000 jobs against 65,000 expected; September was revised up to 60,000 and August to 186,000, together 84,000 more than first reported. Unemployment held at 4.1 percent, average hourly earnings rose 3.1 percent on the year against 2.9 expected, and private payrolls added 159,000. Michigan sentiment beat at 51.0 with one-year inflation expectations down to 4.3 percent. The front end gave back half of Thursday's haven rally: the two-year rose six basis points to 4.52, the ten-year two to 4.86, the thirty-year to 5.26; the curve flattened to 34 basis points. December's hike went back to about 70 percent in futures. The ICE dollar index rose 0.72 percent to 102.28, its best day since early October, firmer against all seven currencies in the layer: the Aussie fell 1.2 percent, sterling 0.8, the euro 0.75, and the loonie went to 1.4134. THE BOUNCE WAS IN WHAT FELL. The S&P rose 0.31 percent to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq 1.1 percent as semiconductors recovered about 4 percent of Thursday's 12; the Dow fell 0.5. The equal-weight index fell 0.4 percent — staples, health care and financials slipping from records — the mirror image of Thursday. On the week the S&P lost 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4, its fourth straight weekly fall; technology fell 8 percent and energy 12. Susquehanna estimated 40 percent of planned AI data-centre capacity at delay risk after the election. The VIX eased to 25.64; the Risk leg holds RISK_OFF, 64 cents above its edge. The S&P sits 0.7 percent above its 200-day. Gold slipped 1.2 percent; the TSX rose 0.5. OIL FLAT, THE WEEK DOWN 13 PERCENT. December WTI settled 90.83 and Brent's January 98.32, closing the largest weekly fall since 2022. Bloomberg reports Saudi and Emirati crude shipments back to prewar levels, Riyadh's Asian prices at a six-year discount, and Washington and Tehran moving closer to a breakthrough; CIBC's Babin calls the market 'wait-and-see'. The fair-value reference reads 91.67 — January constructed a fifth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $1.67 above the $90 edge: Supply PERSISTENT, Cost-Push / Hawkish Pivot at tenure two. The oil channel stays off; two of four. The hysteresis layer's first shadow session agrees with the published label. HELD 10/4/76/10. Saudi air defences intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Najran and a drone over Mecca — a repeat intercept; ledger 80/7/5/0. The tanker hit north of Qatar on Wednesday cost a crew member's life, its operator confirmed. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed two more tankers on mines, unverified for a fifth time in six days. An Iranian nuclear proposal via Qatar was reported without a named source; the AP reports mediators discussing an end to strait attacks in exchange for lifting the blockade. The President said the US may have to 'destroy' the rest of Iran and would decide soon, and spoke with Qatar's Emir about de-escalation. None of it moves the weights. TENURE TWO, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 205. Next: CPI Tuesday; the official Treasury curve Monday; whether the Gulf supply return drives December below $90 decisively.

editions.strategist_view: A blowout payrolls print and an 84,000 upward revision took back half of Thursday's rally in the front end and gave the dollar its best day in a month, which is the Hawkish Pivot half of the label doing exactly what it says. The Cost-Push half is thinner every day: Gulf barrels are back at prewar levels, Saudi Arabia is discounting into Asia, and the reference is $1.67 from the edge. The first shadow session of the hysteresis layer agrees with the published label. Tenure two.
editions.macro_view_client: October payrolls rose 165,000 against 65,000 expected, with upward revisions, and unemployment held at 4.1%; two-year yields rose six basis points and a December Fed hike is again priced near 70%. The dollar index rose 0.7% to 102.3, its best day since early October. Stocks bounced modestly, led by semiconductors; the S&P fell 2.7% on the week. Oil was flat — WTI $90.83 — after its largest weekly fall since 2022 as Gulf shipments returned to prewar levels. COST-PUSH / HAWKISH PIVOT, second day; two of four conditions met. Scenarios unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: OIL BROKE $90. December WTI settled 86.85, down 4.4 percent, and Brent's January 92.57, down 5.9 percent and lower still after the close — the lowest since late August, on top of Brent's 16 percent fall last week. The President told CNN that renewed strikes on Iran were 'highly unlikely' if talks progress; Qatar's prime minister was due at the White House with a reported bridge proposal — the strait reopened and tanker attacks halted in exchange for a lifted port blockade and about $8 billion of frozen funds; Al Arabiya reported arrangements for inspectors to return. UBS and JPMorgan point to a physical surplus. The fair-value reference reads 87.51 — January constructed a sixth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $2.49 below the $90 edge, and December itself is $3.15 below: Supply leaves PERSISTENT and the composite reads Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure one. It is the third crossing of that edge in four sessions; this one is not marginal. The oil channel stays off; two of four. RELIEF RALLY, BROAD THIS TIME. The S&P rose 2.35 percent to 7,549.94, the Dow 1,104 points to 52,389.75, the Nasdaq 2.7 percent, the Russell 3.2. All eleven sectors rose; industrials, technology and discretionary gained about 3 percent and energy lagged. The equal-weight index rose 2.27 percent, within 8 basis points of the cap-weighted one. Nvidia fell to its lowest since April as its board opened an inquiry involving its chief executive, while AMD and Alphabet's chip news lifted the rest of the group. The VIX fell 22 percent to 19.92; the Risk leg leaves RISK_OFF for RISK_TRANSITIONAL. The S&P is 3.0 percent above its 200-day. The TSX rose 1.8 percent. RATES DID NOT JOIN IN. The two-year rose five basis points to 4.56, the ten-year to 4.87, the thirty-year to 5.28. A $58 billion three-year auction cleared at 4.627 percent with a 2.53 bid-to-cover against a 2.64 six-month average. Fed funds futures put a December hike at 84 percent ahead of Tuesday's CPI, where the headline is expected at 0.3 percent on the month after 0.6. The ICE dollar index fell 0.61 percent to 101.68, giving back Friday: the euro rose 0.8 percent, sterling 0.7, the Aussie 0.9; the loonie barely moved at 1.4122. Gold rose 1.7 percent to 4,134. HELD 10/4/76/10 — NOTHING WAS SIGNED. Over the weekend US forces disabled the tanker Huda and a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman enforcing the blockade; UKMTO reported a projectile strike on a vessel leaving the strait and a tanker on fire off Khasab; Saudi commands intercepted at least four missiles over Riyadh and Eastern Province and confirmed shrapnel damage to an Aramco office building; a drone struck Iraq's Khor Mor gas plant. Four repeat entries; ledger 84/7/5/0. Iran's guard claimed two more vessels on mines, unverified. The proposal and Tehran's reported sign-off rest on anonymous diplomats; the Secretary of State called Iran's demands 'outrageous' and said the sides were not close. The oil market priced the words; the weights wait for an act. FIRST RUN WITH THE COMMODITY AND GEOGRAPHIC LAYERS. TENURE ONE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 206. Next: CPI Tuesday 08:30; whether Qatar's visit produces a text; whether December holds below $90.

editions.summary: THE INFLATION TEST CAME BACK HOT WITH OIL FALLING. October's CPI rose 0.4 percent on the month against 0.3 expected, and core 0.3 against 0.2 — the third 0.3 in a row and exactly the reading Governor Waller had said would make a half-point December hike something to consider. Energy rose only 0.7 percent after September's 5.2; shelter rose 0.3 and supplied about a third of the increase; food rose 0.5; used cars fell 1.2. The statistics bureau published no twelve-month rates because October 2025 was never collected, so the 3.7 percent headline and 2.6 core are held from September and say so. THE FRONT END REPRICED. The official Treasury curve — taken same-day from the Treasury's own table — put the two-year at 4.73, up 17 basis points, the five-year at 4.81, the ten-year at 4.98, up 10, and the thirty-year at 5.35, up 9; the two-to-ten gap narrowed to 25 basis points from 32. A ten-year auction cleared at 5.02. FedWatch has December fully priced: 85 to 88 percent for a quarter-point and 11 to 15 for a half, from 1 before the print; a cumulative 50 by January is 49 percent. Daly said policy will need to tighten further and Hammack asked for more frequent moves. The ICE dollar index rose 0.57 percent to 102.24: the euro fell 0.5 percent, sterling 0.7, the Aussie 0.8; the yen weakened to 158.78 and the loonie to 1.4180. Gold fell 2.5 percent to 4,030. The bond market is closed Wednesday; a $25 billion thirty-year auction follows Thursday. STOCKS FELL, NARROWLY. The S&P lost 0.38 percent to 7,520.93, the Dow 158 points to 52,231.89, the Nasdaq 0.74 percent, the Russell 0.68. Technology fell 1.2 percent, the weakest of eleven sectors; financials rose 0.5 and six sectors finished higher. Nvidia fell another 5.5 percent to 168.89, its second fall since its board opened an inquiry. Inside the S&P 500, 246 members rose and 250 fell, and the equal-weight index was flat — 35 basis points ahead of the cap-weighted one; across all US issues 61 percent declined and new lows outnumbered highs 308 to 125. The VIX slipped to 19.46. The S&P is 2.6 percent above its 200-day. The TSX fell 0.76 percent. OIL KEPT FALLING AND THE LABEL HELD. December WTI settled 86.04, down 0.9 percent, and Brent's January 91.49, down 1.2, after trading under $90 before dawn for the first time since the end of August. The fair-value reference reads 86.64 — January constructed a seventh time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $3.36 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING and the composite reads Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure two. The oil channel stays off; two of four. JPMorgan puts October's surplus near 1.4 million barrels a day. HELD 10/4/76/10 — NOTHING SIGNED OR EXECUTED. After meeting Qatar's prime minister the President said he is holding off new strikes at the request of Iran's neighbours, 'locked and loaded'; in Paris the Secretary of State saw 'no need' for major combat operations while the economic campaign runs. The port blockade stands. Tehran says its two-day reopening offer remains on its conditions. On the water nothing paused: ADNOC confirmed one of its vessels damaged by an attack in UAE waters, UKMTO reported a tanker struck by a projectile off Oman, and Saudi Arabia confirmed a fire on the East-West pipeline in Medina region — two repeat entries, 86/7/5/0. Guard claims of three tankers on fire, the Qeshm strike reports and the Mildenhall aircraft report count for nothing. FIRST EDITION UNDER RB-1.2.1. TENURE TWO, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 207. Next: bond market closed Wednesday; 30-year auction Thursday; whether Fed speakers endorse a half-point; whether Doha produces a text.

editions.strategist_view: Yesterday's question was whether a firm CPI with crude falling would make the argument domestic. It did. Core printed its third 0.3 while energy rose 0.7, the two-year moved 17bp, and December is fully priced with a half-point no longer a tail. The label is unchanged — Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure two, the reference $3.36 under the edge — but its second word is now doing the work: lower oil is not buying lower rates. Equities took it narrowly; the long end is 35bp over 5%. On Iran the President's restraint is a sentence, the blockade is a fact, and two vessels and a pipeline were hit. Weights unchanged.
editions.macro_view_client: October inflation came in firmer than expected — consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month and core 0.3% for a third time — even as oil kept falling: WTI settled $86.04 and Brent $91.49. Bonds repriced: the two-year yield rose 17 basis points to 4.73%, the ten-year to 4.98%, and a December Fed hike is fully priced, with a 11–15% chance of a half-point. Stocks slipped, the S&P 500 down 0.38%; the dollar rose and gold fell 2.5%. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. President Trump is holding off new strikes on Iran, but nothing has been signed, so scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: A RALLY WITH THE BOND MARKET SHUT. The S&P rose 1.31 percent to 7,619.38, within 2.6 percent of its record; the Nasdaq rose 1.60 percent, the Dow 0.49, the Russell 0.88 and the TSX 0.67. CoreWeave's beat-and-raise quarter revived the AI trade a day after it had been the reason to sell: technology rose 3.2 percent, every member of the Philadelphia semiconductor index finished higher, and Nvidia rose 2.9 percent to 173.73 after losing nearly 10 percent in two sessions. Ten of eleven sectors rose. It was the mirror of Tuesday: the equal-weight index gained 0.80 percent and trailed the cap-weighted one by 51 basis points. Advancers led 1.48 to one on the NYSE; the S&P 500 had 17 new highs and no new lows. The S&P is 3.9 percent above its 200-day. RISK MOVED TO RISK-ON, THINLY. The VIX fell 10 percent to 17.49, a fourth straight decline and half a point under the 18 line, so the Risk tag moves from RISK_TRANSITIONAL to RISK_ON with almost no margin. The composite label does not depend on it: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure three. NO TREASURY MARKET, NO NEW YIELDS. Cash Treasuries were closed for Veterans Day. The two-year at 4.73, the ten-year at 4.98 and the thirty-year at 5.35 are Tuesday's official closes carried forward and say so; the equity rally was not tested against a bond market. Fed speakers did not soften: Goolsbee called October's CPI report 'borderline disturbing', Logan sees two more quarter-point hikes and possibly faster ones this winter, Paulson said further gradual tightening seems appropriate. December stays fully priced, with about 10 percent on a half-point. Thursday brings jobless claims, a $25 billion thirty-year auction and Cisco; Friday, producer prices. THE DOLLAR MADE A THREE-MONTH HIGH AND GOLD LOST 4,000. The ICE dollar index gained 0.68 percent to 102.93, a second rise and its highest close since at least mid-August: the euro fell 0.7 percent to 1.1093, sterling 0.5, the franc 1.0; the yen weakened to 159.85 and the loonie to 1.4248. Gold fell 1.1 percent to 3,987, its first close under 4,000 since 3 November. OIL ROSE AND THE LABEL HELD. December WTI settled 86.53, up 0.6 percent, and Brent's January 92.76, up 1.4, after Tehran's remarks. The fair-value reference reads 87.07 — January constructed an eighth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $2.93 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off; two of four. IRAN DENIED TALKS; WEIGHTS HELD 10/4/76/10. Tehran's security chief called reports of continuing negotiations or a Qatar meeting 'a pure lie', said the strait stays shut until seven conditions are met, and said not 'a single particle' of enriched material will leave the country. The President said the war ends 'when we want to end it' and that new attacks are unnecessary; the Secretary of State is 'open to diplomacy' and rejected reparations. The Guard claimed two more tankers struck mines and burned; no maritime authority or operator has confirmed it, so it is a claim and scores nothing. No act was confirmed today: 86/7/5/0 unchanged. Monitoring firms count at least 37 attacks on ships this month, the most of the war. TENURE THREE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 208. Next: whether Thursday's bond market confirms or reverses the equity read; the thirty-year auction; whether the VIX holds under 18.

editions.strategist_view: Equities took back Tuesday and more, but they did it on a day the Treasury market was shut — the hot CPI has not been retested in bonds, and three Fed speakers leaned harder, not softer. Risk flips to RISK_ON on a VIX half a point under 18; the equal-weight index lagged by 51bp, so this was the AI complex, not the market. The dollar is the cleaner signal: a three-month high at 102.93, yen near 160, gold through 4,000. Label unchanged, tenure three, reference $2.93 under the edge. Tehran denied talks exist; the tanker claims are unconfirmed. Weights unchanged. Thursday's thirty-year auction is the test.
editions.macro_view_client: Stocks rebounded with the bond market closed for Veterans Day: the S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619 and the Nasdaq 1.60% after CoreWeave's results revived AI shares, and the VIX fell to 17.49. Treasury yields shown are Tuesday's — 4.73% two-year, 4.98% ten-year — and a December Fed hike remains fully priced; Fed officials again spoke for higher rates. The dollar rose to a three-month high, gold slipped below $4,000 and oil edged up, WTI settling $86.53 and Brent $92.76. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. Iran denied that talks are under way and nothing has been signed, so scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.
