editions.summary: THE BOND MARKET VOTED, AND IT SOLD. Cash Treasuries reopened after Veterans Day and repriced the inflation report in one session: the two-year rose 13 basis points to 4.86, the five-year 14 to 4.95, the ten-year 12 to 5.10 — back over 5 percent for the first time since 28 October — and the thirty-year 8 to 5.43, on the Treasury's own same-day curve. The $25 billion thirty-year reopening cleared at 5.441 percent, 0.4 basis points through the when-issued level, with bid-to-cover at 2.36, the lowest since June. Fed funds futures price 29 basis points for December — a hike in full and about a one-in-six chance of a half-point. Goolsbee said inflation 'looks like it's going the wrong way'; Hammack wants smaller, more frequent moves; Bowman supports more hikes but is 'in less of a hurry'. Initial claims were 200,000; the four-week average is the lowest since 1969. NVIDIA'S CHIEF EXECUTIVE RESIGNED. Jensen Huang stepped down as president, chief executive and director, disclosed in an 8-K before the open, with chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive; the board had opened an inquiry on 8 November. The stock fell as much as 14 percent and closed down 4.3 percent at 166.19, while AMD and Broadcom rose about 5. The S&P lost 0.35 percent to 7,592.40, the Dow 0.36, the Nasdaq 0.39, the Russell 1.66 and the TSX 0.75; the equal-weight index fell 0.87 percent, trailing by 52 basis points. RISK BACK TO TRANSITIONAL. The VIX rose 7 percent to 18.70, back over the 18 line one session after crossing under it, so the Risk tag returns to RISK_TRANSITIONAL. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure four. OIL JUMPED AND THE SUPPLY EDGE IS CLOSE. December WTI settled 88.74, up 2.6 percent, and Brent's January 95.82, up 3.3, after the President wrote that 'we don't need a deal with Iran' — despite a 4.7 million-barrel US crude build. The fair-value reference reads 89.22 — January constructed a ninth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $0.78 below the $90 edge; December itself is $1.26 below. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off, $5.78 short of $95. The dollar index rose to 103.20, the highest close in the archive; the yen touched 160; gold fell 2.6 percent to 3,884. HELD 10/4/76/10. The Saudi-led coalition destroyed two ballistic missiles aimed at western Saudi Arabia and two drones; debris fell on a village in Makkah Region without casualties — one repeat entry, 87/7/5/0. The Guard's claim of two burning tankers carrying four million barrels has no independent confirmation and scores nothing; a delayed UKMTO notice of a tanker struck on Tuesday may be the incident already counted and is held, not double-counted. The White House says the blockade continues 'with full effect'; Tehran added compensation for environmental damage to its conditions. Nothing was signed. TWO RULINGS RATIFIED. The Hormuz field now follows one series — Kpler's weekly direct crossings, 63.5 percent for the week to 28 October — instead of whichever source printed last; other measures, from 34.5 to 99.9 percent, are recorded beside it but never drive it. The Russell 2000 field takes a wire close checked against the IWM-scaled estimate, with that estimate as the flagged fallback; eight unverified historical values were replaced. No label, tag or weight changed. TENURE FOUR, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 209. Next: Friday's producer prices; whether the reference crosses $90; whether ten-year yields hold above 5%.

editions.summary: PRODUCER PRICES CAME IN SOFTER THAN FEARED, AND YIELDS ROSE ANYWAY. October producer prices rose 0.3 percent against 0.4 expected, core 0.3 percent in line; the annual rate reached 6.5 percent, the highest since November 2022 but below the 6.6 percent forecast, with goods prices up 10.2 percent on the year. The Treasury's same-day curve still moved higher: the two-year to 4.88, the ten-year 5 basis points to 5.15 and the thirty-year to 5.47 — the ten-year about 30 basis points higher over the week. Daly described a bias toward further tightening and Collins said tighter policy is coming; December is fully priced, with about a one-in-ten chance of a half-point. BREADTH POSITIVE UNDER A RED INDEX. The S&P 500 fell 0.40 percent to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq 0.91 percent as technology lost 2 percent — AMD fell 8.8 percent and Nvidia posted a sixth straight weekly decline — yet 314 index members rose against 185 and the equal-weight index gained 0.20 percent, 60 basis points ahead. Staples led with 1.4 percent. The Dow added 0.10 percent, the Russell lost 0.31 and the TSX 0.09. The S&P still gained 2.5 percent on the week. RISK STAYS TRANSITIONAL. The VIX rose 3 percent to 19.30; the composite label is unchanged — Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure five. OIL FLAT, THE EDGE HOLDS. December WTI settled 88.56, down 0.2 percent, and Brent's January 95.84; WTI fell about 2.5 percent on the week. The fair-value reference reads 88.98 — January constructed a tenth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $1.02 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off, $6.02 short of $95. The dollar index set another archive high at 103.41; gold held at 3,876 while silver fell 3 percent. HELD 10/4/76/10. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi drones over the Riyadh area and the Eastern Province — one repeat entry, 88/7/5/0. The Guard's claims that two tankers and a gas carrier hit mines, and that a US early-warning radar in Bahrain was destroyed — denied by CENTCOM — score nothing; reported strikes with unclear dates are held rather than double-counted. CENTCOM says 23 vessels have been turned around; Tehran says the strait stays closed while the blockade lasts; UKMTO counts transits about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels. Nothing was signed. TENURE FIVE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 210. Next: Monday's Empire State survey and Chair Warsh at noon; whether the reference crosses $90; whether ten-year yields keep climbing above 5%.

editions.strategist_view: A softer-than-feared PPI did not buy the bond market any relief: the ten-year added 5bp to 5.15 and closes the week about 30bp higher, which says the market is pricing the hawkish half of the label on persistence, not on any single print. Underneath a red index, breadth was positive — 314 up, equal-weight 60bp ahead — so the selling is concentrated in AI leadership rather than broad de-risking. Oil sat still; the reference is $1.02 from $90 and remains the variable most likely to end tenure. The dollar keeps making archive highs. Weights unchanged: claims, not acts. Monday: Warsh at noon.
editions.macro_view_client: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October, a little softer than expected, but the annual rate of 6.5% is the highest in almost four years and Treasury yields kept climbing: the ten-year ended at 5.15%, about 0.3 points higher on the week. A December Fed hike stays fully priced. Technology shares fell 2% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.4%, yet most stocks rose and the equal-weight index gained 0.2%. Oil was steady at $88.56 for WTI and $95.84 for Brent; the dollar reached a new high for the year. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met, and oil is about a dollar from the level that would change it. Scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: AN AI SELLOFF INTO NVIDIA'S RESULTS. The S&P 500 fell 1.92 percent to 7,416.59, its third straight loss and the biggest three-session drop since June, and the Nasdaq 2.49 percent to 24,509.76 as a semiconductor gauge lost 5.3 percent and Nvidia 4.1 percent a session before its first results since its chief executive resigned. New US rules tightened China's access to advanced chips as the President began a trip to China. The Dow lost 1.41 percent, the Russell 1.70 and the TSX 1.06. The equal-weight index fell 1.01 percent, 91 basis points better than the index — the selling stayed concentrated. VOLATILITY UP, RISK STILL TRANSITIONAL. The VIX rose 19 percent to 22.91, below the 25 line; the composite label is unchanged — Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure six. SOFTER DATA, LOWER YIELDS. The New York Fed's manufacturing index fell to 7.8 against 18 expected and 25.5 in October. The Treasury's same-day curve eased: the two-year 5 basis points to 4.83, the ten-year 3 to 5.12, the thirty-year to 5.46. Chair Warsh said nothing about rates or December; he set out three staff scenarios for AI, labelled not forecasts, including one in which equity valuations fall and the economy slows. A December hike stays fully priced. OIL DOWN 3 PERCENT ON SURPLUS. December WTI settled 85.72, down 2.84, and Brent's January 92.44, down 3.40, as recovering Gulf flows and an IEA fourth-quarter surplus outweighed new tanker incidents. The fair-value reference reads 85.96 — January constructed an eleventh time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $4.04 below the $90 edge, the widest margin of the tenure. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off, $9.04 short of $95. The dollar index set another archive high at 103.59; gold eased to 3,864 and silver fell 3.7 percent. HELD 10/4/76/10. Four repeat entries take the record to 92/7/5/0: UKMTO confirmed the tanker ON PHOENIX was struck by an unknown projectile leaving the strait, with an engine-room fire and no casualties; Bahrain intercepted drones aimed at the Riffa base on Sunday; Saudi Arabia intercepted two Houthi drones; and CENTCOM's Friday statement that it shot down two Iranian drones launched toward Bahrain — logged on Friday only as a denied claim — is counted today. Iranian claims of six tankers on fire and of mines on a southern route score nothing; a second reported engine-room fire is held until UKMTO numbers it. A third US carrier group reached the region. EIA's new quarterly data put third-quarter Hormuz oil flows at 9.1 million barrels a day against 21.4 a year earlier. Nothing was signed. TENURE SIX, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 211. Next: Nvidia's results Tuesday after the close; Wednesday's Fed minutes; whether the strait series updates before it ages out on 19 November.

editions.strategist_view: The tape is doing the hawkish label's work for the Fed: a third day of AI-led selling, VIX near 23, and a soft Empire print pulled two-year yields down 5bp even with December fully priced. Breadth still says concentration, not capitulation — equal-weight beat the index by 91bp. Oil's 3% drop on surplus widens the supply cushion to $4 below $90, the largest of this tenure, so the label is more secure on the energy side than at any point since it began. Four confirmed strikes and interceptions — including a Friday CENTCOM statement we under-counted — moved the record but not the weights. Tuesday: Nvidia.
editions.macro_view_client: Technology shares led a third day of declines: the S&P 500 fell 1.9% and the Nasdaq 2.5% before Nvidia's results on Tuesday, though the average stock fell about half as much as the index. Market volatility rose to its highest level in a week. A weak New York factory survey pulled Treasury yields lower; the Fed chair did not discuss rates, and a December hike is still expected. Oil fell about 3% — WTI $85.72, Brent $92.44 — as Gulf supplies recover, leaving it about $4 below the level that would change our reading. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. Scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: RISK TURNS OFF. The VIX rose 11 percent to 25.46, its fourth straight gain and its first close above 25 since the label began, moving Risk Sentiment from TRANSITIONAL to RISK_OFF — 0.46 beyond the line. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure seven. BROAD SELLING. The S&P 500 fell 1.03 percent to 7,340.53, a fourth straight loss and its lowest close since 29 July, finishing on its 200-day average. The Dow lost 1.64 percent, the Russell 1.50, the TSX 1.14 and the Nasdaq 0.74. Unlike last week, the selling was broad: all eleven sectors fell, only 75 index members rose against 426, and the equal-weight index lagged by 42 basis points. Software led the losses. A report of a classified NSA network outage broke a morning bounce; the agency called it routine maintenance. NVIDIA BEATS AFTER THE BELL. Revenue of $115.8 billion topped the $109.1 billion estimate and the company guided the fourth quarter to about $130 billion against $125.1 billion expected; the shares rose about 3 percent after hours, after today's closes. DATA MIXED, YIELDS LOWER. October retail sales rose 0.2 percent and 0.6 percent excluding autos; manufacturing output rose 0.3 percent; the homebuilders' index fell to 25, a fourteen-year low; import prices excluding petroleum rose 0.8 percent. The Treasury's same-day curve eased: the two-year 3 basis points to 4.80, the ten-year 2 to 5.10, the thirty-year unchanged at 5.46. Musalem said up to four more hikes may be needed by spring; Williams said there is no need for dramatic action. December stays fully priced. High-yield spreads widened 11 basis points to 3.34 percent on Monday. OIL STEADY. December WTI settled 86.01, up 0.29, and Brent's January 93.14, up 0.70, as tanker attacks and an expected US crude draw offset the IEA surplus. The fair-value reference reads 86.19 — January constructed a twelfth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $3.81 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off. The dollar index held its archive high at 103.60; gold fell to 3,847. HELD 10/4/76/10 — MATRIX v3'S FIRST EDITION. Five repeat entries take the record to 97/7/5/0: IRGC drones launched toward Bahrain's Isa Air Base were intercepted without damage (CENTCOM, Bahrain); US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island (US military official; Iranian officials) — the class of the November 3 revision, so a repeat; UKMTO said an attack disabled the LPG tanker TARA GAS north of Khasab and set its engine room alight, crew safe; Kuwait and Saudi Arabia intercepted drones. Iranian claims of a destroyed radar — denied by CENTCOM — and of mines on several tankers score nothing. Quiet clock 0 of 10; class clock 10 of 14. Nothing was signed. TENURE SEVEN, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 212. Next: Nvidia's reception Wednesday; the Fed minutes; Anthropic's IPO pricing; the strait series ages out on 19 November.

editions.strategist_view: The character of the selloff changed today: after a week in which equal-weight beat cap-weight while AI leaders fell, every sector fell, 426 members declined and equal-weight lagged — that is de-risking, not rotation, and the VIX closing above 25 turns Risk Sentiment off for the first time in this tenure. The supply cushion is still $3.81 and Nvidia's beat after the bell may relieve the AI leg, so the composite holds. The conflict produced a US strike on Qeshm, a repeat of the November 3 class; it moved the ledger, not the weights. Watch whether the VIX holds above 25 after Nvidia.
editions.macro_view_client: Stocks fell broadly for a fourth day: the S&P 500 lost 1.0% to its lowest close since July, every sector declined and most stocks fell, and market volatility rose above the level we treat as risk-off. After the close, Nvidia reported results and guidance above expectations. Retail sales rose modestly while the homebuilders' index hit a 14-year low; Treasury yields eased and a December Fed hike is still expected. Oil was steady at $86.01 for WTI and $93.14 for Brent, about $4 below the level that would change our reading. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. Scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: RISK STEPS BACK FROM OFF. The VIX eased 3.5 percent to 24.56, back under the 25 line after a single session above it, moving Risk Sentiment from RISK_OFF to TRANSITIONAL. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure seven. FIFTH STRAIGHT LOSS, BELOW THE 200-DAY. The S&P 500 fell 0.23 percent to 7,323.63, its fifth straight loss and longest losing run since June, and closed 0.31 percent below its 200-day average, the first such close since April. The Dow lost 1.11 percent as health insurers fell on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule, with UnitedHealth the largest drag; the Nasdaq rose 0.42 percent and the Russell 0.46. The TSX fell 2.09 percent with energy and gold miners. Breadth was close to even — 236 index members rose against 265 — and the equal-weight index edged ahead by 10 basis points, so yesterday's broad selling did not extend. NVIDIA FADES ITS BEAT. The shares opened higher on results and guidance above expectations, then reversed to close 2.89 percent lower, a fifth straight loss, while AMD and Broadcom rose. FED MINUTES KEEP HIKES PRICED. The minutes of the last meeting and Governor Waller kept rate-hike expectations firmly in place; December stays fully priced. The dollar index rose to 103.81, a new archive high, and gold fell 3.2 percent to 3,724, its weakest in more than a year. The Treasury's same-day curve eased as oil fell: the two-year unchanged at 4.80, the ten-year down 3 basis points to 5.07, the thirty-year down 5 to 5.41. High-yield spreads widened another 9 basis points to 3.43 percent on Tuesday. OIL FALLS 3 PERCENT. December WTI settled 83.26, down 2.75, and Brent's January 91.95, down 1.19, as a larger-than-expected US inventory build, a firmer dollar and risk aversion outweighed attacks in the Gulf. The fair-value reference reads 83.38 — January constructed a thirteenth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $6.62 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off. December WTI expires on Friday. HELD 10/4/76/10. Three repeat entries take the record to 100/7/5/0: an Emirati tanker was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, with one crew member missing and eleven injured, and Saudi Arabia condemned the attack; UKMTO reported a second tanker struck in its engine room north of Khasab, crew safe; the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi missile aimed at southern Saudi Arabia. A reported drone attack on Kuwait is held as a possible repeat of Tuesday's entry. Iranian claims that three tankers struck mines, and Houthi claims of strikes on Riyadh, score nothing. Quiet clock 0 of 10; class clock 11 of 14. Nothing was signed. TENURE SEVEN, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 213. Next: whether the S&P holds below its 200-day; Anthropic's first trade; December WTI expiry Friday; the strait series ages out on 19 November.

editions.strategist_view: The selling narrowed rather than deepened: breadth went from 75/426 to 236/265, equal-weight beat cap-weight again, and the VIX slipped back under 25, so Risk Sentiment returns to transitional after one session off. What did break is the S&P's 200-day average, on a day Nvidia faded a clean beat and the Fed minutes kept hikes priced. Oil fell 3% to 83.26 despite two tankers hit in the Strait — the supply cushion widens to $6.62 and the composite holds. Watch whether the index reclaims its 200-day before the December WTI expiry on Friday.
editions.macro_view_client: Stocks were mixed: the S&P 500 slipped 0.2% for a fifth straight loss and closed below its 200-day average for the first time since April, while the Nasdaq and small caps rose and the Dow fell 1.1% on health insurers. Nvidia gave up an early gain after its results. Fed minutes kept a December hike fully priced, lifting the dollar and pushing gold down 3.2%. Market volatility eased back below the level we treat as risk-off. Oil fell 3% to $83.26 for WTI and $91.95 for Brent, about $7 below the level that would change our reading. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. Scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: RISK BACK TO OFF. The VIX rose 15.8 percent to 28.44, back above the 25 line one session after dropping below it, so Risk Sentiment returns to RISK_OFF. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure nine. SIXTH STRAIGHT LOSS. Stocks opened higher as Anthropic began trading and reversed through the session. The S&P 500 fell 2.02 percent to 7,175.83, its sixth straight loss and longest losing run since 2024, 8.2 percent below its October record and 2.25 percent under its 200-day average. The Dow lost 2.19 percent and closed below 50,000; the Nasdaq fell 2.25 percent after being up as much as 2 percent; the Russell 2000 fell 2.18 percent and the TSX 1.59 percent. More than nine in ten index members fell; the equal-weight index fell 1.79 percent, 23 basis points less than the cap-weighted index. Nvidia lost 3.3 percent and AMD fell on a short-seller report. YIELDS LOWER, DOLLAR HIGHER. The Treasury's same-day curve fell as stocks sold off: the two-year 4 basis points to 4.76, the ten-year 3 to 5.04, the thirty-year 1 to 5.40. December stays fully priced; Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said he sees no clear path back to 2 percent inflation. The dollar index rose to 103.95, another archive high; gold fell 1.5 percent to 3,667, a 14-month low. High-yield spreads widened 4 basis points to 3.47 percent as of Wednesday, 24 basis points in three sessions. OIL FLAT. December WTI settled 83.21, down 5 cents and the lowest since 26 August; Brent's January settled 91.98, up 3 cents. Tanker reports in the Strait offset a 3.4 million barrel US crude build. The fair-value reference reads 83.27 — January constructed a fourteenth time on the 1.91 spread, provisional — $6.73 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING; the oil channel stays off. December WTI expires on Friday. HELD 10/4/76/10. One repeat entry takes the record to 101/7/5/0: the Saudi-led coalition addressed a Houthi missile threat toward Riyadh, and debris damaged the facade of the Public Investment Fund tower, with no casualties reported. Iran's navy says two tankers hit mines in the Strait; that has not been verified and counts nothing. Wednesday's Kuwait hold is resolved as a repeat of Tuesday's entry. The escalation and resolution anchors came up for review today and were held: fifteen repeat entries since 5 November but no new class, and nothing signed. Quiet clock 0 of 10; class clock 12 of 14. STRAIT SERIES STALE. The canonical strait reading (63.5 percent, week to 28 October) is now 16 business days old, past its 15-day limit, and is held unchanged pending an operator decision; a preliminary Kpler figure through 16 November would read 57.5 percent. Both sit below 70 percent, so the chokepoint condition is unmet either way. TENURE NINE, TWO OF FOUR, 10/4/76/10, DAY 214. Next: December WTI expiry Friday and the January roll; the class clock completes on 23 November if no new class appears; the strait series decision.

editions.strategist_view: Today removed the cushion yesterday's breadth suggested: a full reversal from an early gain, nine in ten stocks down, the S&P six days lower and 2.25% under its 200-day, and the VIX back above 25 — Risk returns to off. The rates market read it as growth risk, not inflation: yields fell while the dollar still made a new high. Oil held at August lows despite tanker attacks, so the composite does not move. Watch whether credit, now 24bp wider in three sessions, starts to lead equities rather than follow them.
editions.macro_view_client: Stocks fell sharply after an early rally faded on Anthropic's first day of trading: the S&P 500 lost 2.0% for a sixth straight decline, the Dow fell 2.2% and closed below 50,000, and the Nasdaq dropped 2.3%. Market volatility rose back above the level we treat as risk-off. Treasury yields fell, the dollar rose to its highest in our record and gold fell to a 14-month low. Oil was little changed at $83.21 for WTI and $91.98 for Brent, about $7 below the level that would change our reading. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met. Scenarios are unchanged: escalation 76%, resolution 10%.

editions.summary: RISK TO ACUTE. The VIX rose 26 percent to 35.89, its first close above 30 since March and above the 35 line, so Risk Sentiment moves from RISK_OFF to RISK_AVERSION_ACUTE. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure ten. From today the hysteresis layer publishes the label; the VIX crossed the line by 0.89 points against a 0.8 band, so the move is published the same day. AI ROUT. The S&P 500 fell 3.70 percent to 6,910.39, its seventh straight loss, 11.6 percent below its October record and 5.9 percent under its 200-day average; the week's 8.6 percent fall is the worst since April 2025. The Nasdaq lost 5.28 percent and is now down for the year; the Dow fell 1.93 percent and joined the S&P in correction; the Russell 2000 fell 2.76 percent and the TSX 2.47 percent. Nvidia fell 14 percent on reports of an SEC accounting probe and Anthropic 9 percent in its second session. Decliners outnumbered advancers 376 to 123 in the S&P; the equal-weight index fell 1.98 percent, 172 basis points less than the cap-weighted index. Energy and utilities rose. HAVEN BID. The Treasury's same-day curve fell and steepened: the two-year 13 basis points to 4.63, the five-year 15 to 4.71, the ten-year 12 to 4.92 and the thirty-year 9 to 5.31. December hike pricing eased to about 96 percent from fully priced. The yen and Swiss franc rose about 0.7 percent; the dollar index was little changed at 103.84; gold fell 4.0 percent to 3,521. High-yield spreads were 3.52 percent on Thursday, 29 basis points wider in four sessions. DECEMBER WTI EXPIRES. December WTI settled 83.98, up 77 cents, on its last trading day; Brent's January settled 92.57. Both fell for a third week. On the last trading day the reference equals the expiring contract, 83.98, $6.02 below the $90 edge; Supply stays EASING and the oil channel stays off. The reference moves to January on Monday. HELD 10/4/76/10. Two repeat entries take the record to 103/7/5/0: a tanker leaving the Strait was struck by an unknown projectile eight nautical miles north of Khasab and caught fire, and the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile and drones over the south and Riyadh. A reported US strike near Qeshm and reported Iranian fire at a US jet are held until confirmed. The escalation and resolution anchors were ratified as proposed. Quiet clock 0 of 10; class clock 13 of 14. STRAIT FIGURE RECONCILED. On the operator's ruling the strait series moves to Kpler's latest weekly direct-crossing print, 5.66 million barrels a day through the strait in the week to 11 November, 71.7 percent disrupted on the 20 million barrel basis. That is above 70 percent, but under the ratified scope guard it does not count toward the chokepoint condition until a same-scope Kpler baseline confirms it; counted conditions stay two of four. TENURE TEN, TWO OF FOUR COUNTED, 10/4/76/10, DAY 215. Next: the January roll on Monday; the class clock completes Monday if no new class appears; whether credit follows equities.

editions.summary: RISK EASES. The VIX fell 25.8 percent to 26.62, 8.38 points below the 35 line, so Risk Sentiment moves from RISK_AVERSION_ACUTE back to RISK_OFF; the margin is far beyond the 0.8 band, so the hysteresis layer publishes the move the same day. The dollar index closed back above 104, lifting Dollar Regime from USD_FIRM to USD_STRONG by a narrow margin, and the rebound lifted Market Structure from TECHNICAL_BREAKDOWN to TECHNICAL_NEUTRAL. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure eleven. RELIEF RALLY. The S&P 500 rose 4.73 percent to 7,237.17, its best day since April 2025, ending a seven-session losing streak; it is still 7.4 percent below its October record and 1.5 percent under its 200-day average. The Nasdaq rose 6.51 percent, the Dow 3.01 percent, the Russell 2000 3.40 percent and the TSX 2.69 percent. Nvidia rose 31.5 percent after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive; the President said he had persuaded the board, and the company's filing cites senior levels of the US government. Advancers led decliners 417 to 83 in the S&P, but the equal-weight index rose only 2.59 percent, 214 basis points behind the cap-weighted index: a rebound led by the largest names. RATES STILL. The Treasury's same-day curve barely moved: the two-year held at 4.63, the ten-year at 4.92, and the thirty-year eased 2 basis points to 5.29. December hike pricing stayed near 96 percent. The dollar index rose 0.49 percent to 104.32 as the euro fell 0.6 percent; the yen and franc gave back part of Friday's gains. Gold rose 3.5 percent to 3,643 after Friday's liquidation. High-yield spreads were 3.76 percent on Friday, 24 basis points wider on the day and 53 wider in five sessions; Monday's print follows. ROLL TO JANUARY. The oil reference moves to January WTI, which settled 80.17; February settled 79.07. With 28 days to the January expiry, the reference is 80.17 plus 1.10 times 28/30, or 81.20, $8.80 below the $90 edge; Supply stays EASING and the oil channel stays off. Brent's January settled 89.37, its lowest since early September, as Gulf supply recovers, Libya's Sharara field restarts and strike expectations fade. The reference is 22.9 percent below its level thirty days ago. REVISION #28: 10/8/72/10. Three repeat entries take the record to 106/7/6/0: on Saturday two outbound tankers were struck north and east of Khasab, one catching fire; an Iranian strike set a civilian industrial facility at Sitra, Bahrain, on fire and injured two; and the coalition intercepted a Houthi missile over the western region. A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran; Iran says these are not yet formal negotiations, so they are logged as contact only. Houthi, IRGC and mine claims score zero; an incident involving military forces near Chabahar is held until its nature is confirmed; threats to sink blockade runners and to resume strikes after New Year are words. CLASS CLOCK COMPLETE. Fourteen sessions have passed without a new act class, completing the class clock and triggering the registry's mandatory stalemate/escalation review. The review found the conflict running on repeat classes only — the profile of the stalemate cell, Attritional equilibrium — and recommended the indicative 10/8/72/10. The operator ratified it the same evening as revision #28: stalemate rises from 4 to 8 and escalation falls from 76 to 72; base and resolution stay at 10. A new act class would restart the clock and re-open escalation. Quiet clock 0 of 10. STRAIT. The strait series stays at Kpler's week-to-11-November print, 71.7 percent disrupted, now eight sessions old; it is not counted toward the chokepoint condition until a same-scope baseline confirms it. Counted conditions stay two of four. TENURE ELEVEN, TWO OF FOUR COUNTED, 10/8/72/10 (#28), DAY 216. Next: whether a new act class re-opens escalation; whether the rebound broadens beyond the largest names; Monday's credit print.

editions.summary: ROTATION. The S&P 500 fell 0.50 percent to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq 1.48 percent as chipmakers gave back part of Monday's surge, while the Dow rose 0.85 percent to 50,018.70, back above 50,000, and the Russell 2000 rose 0.57 percent. The TSX slipped 0.35 percent. The dollar index fell back below 104, so Dollar Regime returns from USD_STRONG to USD_FIRM. The S&P is 1.95 percent under its 200-day average, five basis points inside the line at which Market Structure would turn to TECHNICAL_BREAKDOWN; it stays TECHNICAL_NEUTRAL. Risk Sentiment stays RISK_OFF with the VIX at 26.36. The composite label is unchanged: Disinflation / Hawkish Pivot, tenure twelve. CHIP GIVE-BACK. Nvidia fell 5.9 percent to 155.38, giving back about a quarter of Monday's 31.5 percent gain; the semiconductor fund fell 7.3 percent and Micron 11 percent, and the technology sector lost 3.3 percent. Health care rose 3.0 percent and consumer staples 1.7 percent. The equal-weight index rose 0.54 percent, 104 basis points ahead of the cap-weighted index: Monday's narrow rally reversed into a broad rotation away from the largest names. NYSE breadth was close to even. RATES STILL. The Treasury's same-day curve was again little changed: the two-year held at 4.63 for a third session, the ten-year eased one basis point to 4.91 and the thirty-year rose one to 5.30. Futures price a December hike of 25 basis points at about 95 percent, with the remainder on 50. The Conference Board consumer index rose to 103.3, its highest in nearly two years. The dollar index fell 0.48 percent to 103.82; the euro and sterling rose about 0.6 percent. Gold fell 2.4 percent to 3,556. High-yield spreads tightened 13 basis points to 3.63 percent on Monday. OIL REBOUNDS. January WTI settled 82.05, up 1.88, and February 81.07; with 27 days to the January expiry the reference is 82.05 plus 0.98 times 27/30, or 82.93, $7.07 below the $90 edge. Supply stays EASING and the oil channel stays off. Brent's January settled 91.40, up 2.03. Both contracts touched their lowest since late August during the session before new attacks on ships in the strait lifted them. The reference is 21.3 percent below its level thirty days ago. 10/8/72/10 HELD. Two repeat entries take the record to 108/7/6/0. The UK maritime agency reported that three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles while sailing east through the strait on Monday; they continued their transit. On Tuesday a Houthi strike hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district, injuring 11 people, the second strike on the building in under a week. Iranian claims that three to six tankers hit mines, and that a container ship was targeted, score zero. A report that US forces struck a tanker carrying Iranian oil is held until an official statement confirms it; so is the US investigation into cyberattacks on about 50 tankers. Qatar stepped up efforts to revive US-Iran talks, while Iran said it would not negotiate until seven conditions are met; contacts and words score zero. FIRST SESSION UNDER REVISION #28. The weights ratified on Monday evening — stalemate 8, escalation 72 — hold. No new act class appeared today; a new class would re-open escalation. Quiet clock 0 of 10. STRAIT. The strait series stays at Kpler's week-to-11-November print, 71.7 percent disrupted, now nine sessions old; vessel counts from other trackers point to lower traffic in mid-November but measure a different scope. The reading is not counted toward the chokepoint condition until a same-scope baseline confirms it. Counted conditions stay two of four. TENURE TWELVE, TWO OF FOUR COUNTED, 10/8/72/10, DAY 217. Next: Wednesday's October PCE inflation report; whether the S&P holds above the 200-day line; the S&P 500 member breadth count.
